3.1Chapter 3 · LLM-Based Applications

LLM applications ke types — sirf chatbot nahi

LLM applications 4 bade types me batte hain: simple chat, RAG, agents aur multimodal. Har type ki complexity, cost aur LLMOps needs alag hain — sahi type chunna pehla architectural decision hai.

Upar wali figure generative AI ki growth dikhati hai — adoption itni tez hai ki applications ke types bhi har saal badal rahe hain. Aaj jo "advanced" hai, wo kal "basic" hoga.

Type 1 — Simple LLM apps (prompt in, text out)

Chatbot, summarizer, translator — user prompt bhejta hai, model jawaab deta hai. Sabse simple, sabse sasta, sabse aasan deploy karna. Limitation: model ko tumhara private data nahi pata, aur wo hallucinate kar sakta hai.

Type 2 — RAG apps (retrieval-augmented)

Model jawaab dene se pehle tumhare documents se relevant information retrieve karta hai, phir use context me jawaab deta hai. Accuracy aur trust dono badhte hain. Zyadatar enterprise apps isi type ki hain. Detail Chapter 5 me.

Type 3 — Agentic apps

Agents sirf jawaab nahi dete — plan banate hain, tools use karte hain, multi-step kaam karte hain. Example: "Mere liye kal ki meeting ke liye report banao" — agent calendar dekhega, documents padhega, report banayega aur bhej dega. Sabse powerful, sabse mushkil — evaluation aur reliability ki sabse badi challenge yahi hai.

Type 4 — Multimodal apps

Text ke saath image, audio, video bhi handle karne wale apps — jaise image dekh kar describe karna, ya voice se baat karna. Aage section 3.6 me detail hai.

Konsa type chunna hai

Agar tumhe chahiye...To chunno
Quick demo ya simple Q&ASimple LLM app
Apne data par accurate jawaabRAG app
Multi-step kaam automate karnaAgentic app
Image/voice bhi chahiyeMultimodal app

Rule: sabse simple type se shuru karo jo kaam kar jaye. Agent tabhi banao jab RAG se kaam na chale — agents ki debugging aur evaluation 10x mushkil hai.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 3: LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous2.7 · LLMOps Maturity Model — tum kis level par hoNext →3.2 · Agents aur agentic workflows — LLM jo kaam karta hai
3.2Chapter 3 · LLM-Based Applications

Agents aur agentic workflows — LLM jo kaam karta hai

Agent ek LLM-powered system hai jo ek goal ko achieve karne ke liye khud plan banata hai, tools use karta hai aur steps execute karta hai — bina har step par human ke bataye.

Agent ke 4 core components

  • LLM (brain): reasoning aur planning karta hai — agla step kya hona chahiye.
  • Tools: bahari duniya se interact karne ke tareeke — web search, calculator, database query, API calls, file operations. Tools ke bina agent sirf baat kar sakta hai, kaam nahi.
  • Memory: pehle ke steps aur facts ko yaad rakhna — short-term (current conversation) aur long-term (past interactions, user preferences).
  • Planning: bade task ko chhote steps me todna, steps ko order karna, aur agar koi step fail ho to plan badalna.

Agentic workflow kaise chalta hai

  1. Goal milta hai: user kehta hai "Q3 ki sales report banao".
  2. Planning: agent plan banata hai — data nikalo, analyze karo, chart banao, report likho.
  3. Tool use: agent database se data nikalta hai, analysis tool chalata hai.
  4. Observation: har tool ka result dekh kar agent decide karta hai — aage badho ya plan badlo.
  5. Completion: final output user ko do, ya agar atak jaye to human ko escalate karo.

Agents ki mushkilein — kitab khul kar batati hai

  • Planning weak hai: bahut kam agents abhi tak achhi planning karte hain. Multi-step tasks me wo bhatak jate hain ya galat step le lete hain.
  • Reproducibility nahi hai: agar agent 10-step task ke step 6 par fail ho, to dobara chalane par wo step 3 par fail ho sakta hai ya poora succeed kar sakta hai — koi clear "stack trace" nahi hota.
  • Memory bottleneck hai: facts ko store aur retrieve karna — vectorized ho ya tokenized — latency aur accuracy dono me bottleneck banta hai. Zyadatar memory systems brittle, leaky aur model ki representation se misaligned hote hain.
  • Context bhool jana: lambi tasks me agent pehle ke decisions bhool jata hai.
  • Cost: har step ek LLM call hai — 10-step task matlab 10x cost, aur har retry usse aur badhata hai.
Practical advice: agents ko narrow, well-defined tasks do — "poora project manage karo" nahi, "ye 3 steps karo aur result do" haan. Har agent ke liye human escalation path zaroor rakho.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 3: LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous3.1 · LLM applications ke types — sirf chatbot nahiNext →3.3 · Model Context Protocol (MCP) — LLM ko tools se jodne ka standard
3.3Chapter 3 · LLM-Based Applications

Model Context Protocol (MCP) — LLM ko tools se jodne ka standard

MCP ek open protocol hai jo LLM applications ko external tools aur data sources se standard tareeke se jodta hai. Isse pehle har tool ka alag integration likhna padta tha — MCP ne use "USB port" jaisa standard bana diya: ek baar MCP support kar do, koi bhi compliant tool jud jayega.

MCP ke components

  • MCP Host: wo application jo LLM ko run karti hai — jaise ek AI assistant ya IDE. Host connection manage karta hai.
  • MCP Client: Host ke andar ka component jo ek MCP Server se baat karta hai — one-to-one connection.
  • MCP Server: wo program jo tools, resources aur prompts expose karta hai — jaise ek database server ya file-system server.
  • Tools: wo actions jo model call kar sakta hai — jaise "database query karo" ya "file padho".
  • Resources: wo data jo model padh sakta hai — jaise files ya documents.
  • Prompts: reusable prompt templates jo server provide karta hai.

MCP kaam kaise karta hai — 3 phases

  1. Handshake phase: client aur server apni capabilities exchange karte hain — kaun kya kar sakta hai, protocol version kya hai.
  2. Discovery phase: client server se poochhta hai ki kaun se tools aur resources available hain.
  3. Interaction phase: model tool call karta hai, server execute karta hai, result wapas aata hai, model use apne jawaab me use karta hai.

MCP example project — kitab ka example

Kitab ek example project deti hai jisme ek MCP server banaya jata hai jo ek simple tool expose karta hai. Flow ye hai: server start karo, wo apne tools announce karta hai, client connect hota hai, model user ke sawaal ke hisaab se tool choose karta hai, server tool chalata hai aur result wapas bhejta hai. Tum is pattern ko apne tools par apply kar sakte ho — database, internal APIs, file systems, kuch bhi.

# MCP ka concept — illustrative sketch (Python)
# 1. Server: ek tool expose karo
#    tool: get_customer_orders(customer_id) -> orders ki list
# 2. Client: server se connect karo, tools discover karo
# 3. Model: user ke sawaal par tool call kare, result se jawaab banaye
# Flow: User -> Host/Client -> MCP Server (tool) -> result -> Model -> User

MCP ki mushkilein

  • Security: tool ko kya permissions hain? Ek compromised tool poori system ko nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai — tools ko least-privilege par chalao.
  • Discovery overload: bahut saare tools hone par model galat tool choose kar sakta hai — tools ke descriptions clear aur distinct hone chahiye.
  • Latency: har tool call ek network round-trip hai — chain of tools slow ho sakta hai.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 3: LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous3.2 · Agents aur agentic workflows — LLM jo kaam karta haiNext →3.4 · Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A) — agents aapas me kaise baat karte hain
3.4Chapter 3 · LLM-Based Applications

Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A) — agents aapas me kaise baat karte hain

Jab ek agent ka kaam dusre agent ke kaam par depend kare, to unhe aapas me baat karni padti hai. A2A protocol isi ke liye hai — agents ke beech standard communication, chahe wo alag frameworks ya alag companies ke bane hon.

A2A interaction ke steps

  1. Discovery: ek agent dusre agent ko discover karta hai — wo kya kar sakta hai, uski capabilities kya hain (agent card ke through).
  2. Task bhejna: pehla agent dusre ko ek task bhejta hai — goal, context aur expected output ke saath.
  3. Execution: dusra agent task karta hai — use apne tools aur apni planning se.
  4. Updates: lambi task me progress updates aate hain — "kaam chal raha hai, 50% hua".
  5. Result: final result ya artifacts wapas aate hain — pehla agent unhe apne kaam me use karta hai.

A2A kahan kaam aata hai

  • Multi-agent systems: ek research agent data ikattha kare, ek analysis agent analyze kare, ek writing agent report likhe — teeno alag agents, ek workflow.
  • Cross-company: tumhara agent partner company ke agent se baat kare — jaise ek booking agent, ek payment agent se.
  • Specialization: har agent apne domain me expert ho — general agent banane se behtar hai specialized agents ko jodna.

A2A ki mushkilein

  • Trust: dusre agent par kitna bharosa karein? Uska output verify kaise karein?
  • Error propagation: ek agent ki galti pure chain me failti hai — har handoff par validation chahiye.
  • Cost aur latency: har agent interaction LLM calls badhata hai.
  • Standard abhi naya hai: ecosystem abhi ban raha hai — aaj ka implementation kal badal sakta hai.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 3: LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous3.3 · Model Context Protocol (MCP) — LLM ko tools se jodne ka standardNext →3.5 · MCP vs A2A — farq samjho, dono kab chahiye
3.5Chapter 3 · LLM-Based Applications

MCP vs A2A — farq samjho, dono kab chahiye

MCP aur A2A dono "connection" ke protocol hain, lekin alag levels par. Confuse mat karo — ye competitors nahi, complements hain.

DimensionMCPA2A
ConnectsLLM ↔ Tools / DataAgent ↔ Agent
Sawaal"Model ko ye tool kaise use karne doon?""Ye agent us agent se kaise baat kare?"
ExampleAssistant database se orders nikaleResearch agent, analysis agent ko task de
ScopeEk application ke andarApplications/organizations ke beech
Standard bodyOpen protocol, tezi se adopt ho raha haiNaya standard, ecosystem ban raha hai

Dono ek saath kaise kaam karte hain

Ek typical multi-agent system me: har agent apne tools se MCP ke through judta hai, aur agents aapas me A2A ke through baat karte hain. MCP = agent ki "haath" (tools), A2A = agents ki "baatchit". Tumhe dono ki zaroorat pad sakti hai — ya sirf ek ki, apne use case ke hisaab se.

Infrastructure applications ki mushkilein (aam taur par)

  • Tool sprawl: tools badhte jate hain — unhe catalog, version aur retire karna ek Ops kaam hai.
  • Auth aur permissions: har tool ko kiski credentials milengi? Har agent ko kya karne ki permission hai? Ye security design hai (Chapter 8).
  • Observability: tool calls aur agent interactions ko log karna padta hai — nahi to debug karna impossible hai (Chapter 7).
  • Versioning: tool ka behavior badle to agents ka behavior bhi badlega — tool versions ko model versions ki tarah manage karo.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 3: LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous3.4 · Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A) — agents aapas me kaise baat karte hainNext →3.6 · Multimodal LLMs — text ke aage: image, audio, video
3.6Chapter 3 · LLM-Based Applications

Multimodal LLMs — text ke aage: image, audio, video

Multimodal LLMs sirf text nahi, image, audio aur video bhi samajh sakte hain — aur kabhi-kabhi generate bhi kar sakte hain. Ye LLM applications ka agla frontier hai.

Multimodal kaise kaam karta hai

Har modality ka apna encoder hota hai — image encoder photo ko vectors me badalta hai, audio encoder awaaz ko, text encoder text ko. Phir ye vectors ek shared space me aate hain, jahan LLM unhe ek saath samajh sakta hai. Isi liye model ek photo dekh kar uske baare me likh sakta hai, ya ek voice note sun kar uska jawaab de sakta hai.

Multimodal use cases

  • Image understanding: photo me kya hai describe karo, document scan karke data nikalo, chart padh kar samjhao.
  • Visual Q&A: "Is X-ray me kya dikh raha hai?" — healthcare, manufacturing inspection.
  • Voice assistants: bolo, suno, jawaab do — hands-free kaam, accessibility.
  • Video analysis: meeting recording se summary, security footage se events.
  • Cross-modal search: text se image dhoondo, ya image se similar images.

Multimodal ki khaas challenges

  • Embeddings alag hain: text aur image embeddings ko align karna mushkil hai — galat alignment se galat jawaab aate hain.
  • Data aur cost: multimodal data bada hota hai, training aur inference dono mehenga hota hai.
  • Evaluation mushkil: image wale jawaab ki quality kaise naapo? Text metrics kaafi nahi hain.
  • Security nayi hai: image me chhupa hua prompt injection (ek photo me likha malicious instruction) — ye ek naya attack vector hai.

Kab multimodal chunna hai

Tab jab tumhara use case text-only se solve na ho — jaise documents scan karne hain, ya voice interface chahiye. Agar text se kaam chal jaye, to text se shuru karo — multimodal complexity aur cost dono badhata hai.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 3: LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous3.5 · MCP vs A2A — farq samjho, dono kab chahiyeNext →3.7 · Model chunna aur performance measure karna
3.7Chapter 3 · LLM-Based Applications

Model chunna aur performance measure karna

Application ke liye sahi model chunna sirf "sabse bada model" chunna nahi hai. Kitab ek practical approach batati hai: apne use case ke metrics tay karo, phir models ko un par test karo.

Performance ke 4 dimensions

  • Quality: jawaab kitne sahi aur useful hain? Task ke hisaab se metric chuno — classification me precision/recall, generation me human ya LLM-based eval (Chapter 7).
  • Latency: pehla token kitni der me aata hai (time-to-first-token) aur poora jawaab kitni der me? Real-time chat me ye sabse important hai.
  • Throughput: system ek second me kitne requests handle kar sakta hai? Batch jobs me ye matter karta hai.
  • Cost: per-request cost kitni hai? API ho ya self-hosted — dono ka total cost of ownership nikalo.

AUC-PR example — ek metric kyun kaafi nahi

Upar wali figure ek example dikhati hai jahan AUC-PR (Area Under Precision-Recall Curve) accuracy se behtar predictor hai. Jab classes imbalanced hon — jaise 100 me se 5 hi positive cases hon — to accuracy dhokha deti hai: sabko "negative" bol do, 95% accuracy mil jayegi, lekin ek bhi positive case nahi pakdoge. AUC-PR precision aur recall ke trade-off ko ek number me dikhata hai, isliye imbalanced tasks me ye zyada imaandar metric hai.

Retrieval metrics — RAG ke liye

  • Hit rate (top-k accuracy): kitni baar sahi document top-k results me aaya? Agar k=5 hai aur sahi doc 100 me se 80 baar top-5 me hai, to hit rate 80% hai.
  • MAP (Mean Average Precision): ranking ki quality — sahi docs upar aaye ya neeche?
  • MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank): pehla sahi result kis rank par aaya? Rank 1 par aaye to score 1, rank 2 par aaye to 0.5.

Model chunne ka practical process

  1. Apna eval set banao: 50-100 real examples — apne data se, apne users se.
  2. 2-3 models ko test karo: chhota model bhi try karo — aksar chhota model fine-tune karke bade se behtar aur 10x sasta nikalta hai.
  3. Quality + latency + cost — teeno dekho: sirf quality par decide mat karo.
  4. Champion-challenger rakho: production me ek model (champion) chalao, dusre ko shadow me test karte raho — jab challenger behtar ho, switch karo.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 3: LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous3.6 · Multimodal LLMs — text ke aage: image, audio, videoNext →4.1 · Data engineering kya hai aur LLM ke liye kyun zaroori hai
4.1Chapter 4 · Data Engineering for LLMs

Data engineering kya hai aur LLM ke liye kyun zaroori hai

LLM ki quality uske data ki quality se tay hoti hai. Data engineering wo kaam hai jo raw data ko model ke khane layak banata hai — collect karo, clean karo, organize karo, aur sahi format me model tak pahunchao. Bina achhi data engineering ke, sabse achha model bhi kharab perform karega.

Data engineering ke components

  • Data sources: kahan se data aayega — internal databases, documents, APIs, web, user interactions. Har source ki apni format aur quality hoti hai.
  • Ingestion: data ko source se nikal kar pipeline me lana — batch (daily dump) ya streaming (real-time).
  • Storage: raw data kahan rakho — data lake, data warehouse, vector database. Har ek ka apna use hai.
  • Processing: cleaning, dedup, filtering, transformation — raw se usable tak.
  • Embeddings aur indexing: text ko vectors me badalna aur search ke liye index banana — RAG ki neev.
  • Governance: data lineage (data kahan se aaya), access control, PII handling — Chapter 8 se juda hua.

LLM data, traditional ML data se kaise alag hai

AspectTraditional MLLLM
FormatStructured tables, labeledUnstructured text, mostly unlabeled
VolumeMBs–GBsGBs–TBs, trillions of tokens
Quality issuesMissing values, outliersDuplicates, toxic content, PII, bias, outdated info
Pipeline outputFeature vectorsTokens, embeddings, chunks, indexes

Data engineering ke bina kya hota hai

Kachra data andar jaye to kachra behavior bahar aata hai — model biased, outdated ya toxic output deta hai, RAG galat documents retrieve karta hai, fine-tuning galat seekhta hai. Data par kharch kiya gaya ek ghanta, model debugging ke 10 ghante bachata hai.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 4: Data Engineering for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous3.7 · Model chunna aur performance measure karnaNext →4.2 · LLM training pipeline — pretrain se fine-tune tak
4.2Chapter 4 · Data Engineering for LLMs

LLM training pipeline — pretrain se fine-tune tak

LLM training ek pipeline hai — data collect karo, model ko general knowledge sikhao (pretraining), phir use apne task ke liye dhalo (fine-tuning). Har stage me data ki role alag hoti hai.

Pipeline ke stages

  1. Data collection: diverse sources se massive text ikattha karo — books, articles, websites, code, domain documents.
  2. Data cleaning: duplicates hatao, toxic aur low-quality content filter karo, PII remove karo, language detect karo.
  3. Tokenization: text ko tokens me todo — model tokens par train hota hai, words par nahi.
  4. Pretraining: model agla word predict karna seekhta hai — general language aur knowledge.
  5. Fine-tuning: task-specific data par model ko aur train karo — instruction following, domain knowledge.
  6. Alignment: human feedback se model ka behavior sudharo — helpful, honest, harmless.
  7. Evaluation: har stage par test karo — benchmarks, apna eval set, human review (Chapter 7).

Har stage par data ki alag need

  • Pretraining data: bada, diverse, general — quality matters, lekin scale bhi matters.
  • Fine-tuning data: chhota, high-quality, task-specific — 1,000 achhe examples 100,000 bekaar examples se behtar hain.
  • Evaluation data: bilkul alag hona chahiye training data se — nahi to tum khud ko dhokha de rahe ho (data contamination).
Data contamination se bacho: agar tumhara test data training data me leak ho gaya, to model test par achha dikhega lekin real duniya me fail hoga. Train aur test data ko sakhti se alag rakho — aur decontamination check karo.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 4: Data Engineering for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous4.1 · Data engineering kya hai aur LLM ke liye kyun zaroori haiNext →4.3 · Data Engineering Lifecycle (DELC) — 5 stages
4.3Chapter 4 · Data Engineering for LLMs

Data Engineering Lifecycle (DELC) — 5 stages

DELC ek framework hai jo batata hai ki data zindagi bhar kaise manage hota hai — janm se lekar retirement tak. LLM ke liye isme 5 stages hain.

5 stages

  1. Generation: data paida hota hai — user interactions, sensors, transactions, documents. Yahan sawal hai: data kahan se aayega aur kis format me?
  2. Storage: data kahan rakha jayega — data lake (raw, cheap), warehouse (structured, queryable), vector DB (embeddings, search). Storage ka faisla access pattern par depend karta hai.
  3. Ingestion: data ko source se storage tak lana — batch ya streaming. Ingestion me schema validation aur error handling zaroori hai.
  4. Transformation: raw data ko usable me badalna — cleaning, dedup, enrichment, tokenization, embedding. Ye sabse zyada mehnat wala stage hai.
  5. Serving: data ko consumers tak pahunchana — model training, RAG retrieval, analytics dashboards. Serving me latency aur freshness matter karti hai.

DELC ke aas-paas ki cheezein (undercurrents)

  • Security: har stage par — encryption, access control, audit logs.
  • Data management: governance, lineage, quality checks — har stage par.
  • DataOps: pipelines ko code ki tarah manage karo — versioning, testing, CI/CD.
  • Data architecture: poora system kaise judta hai — ek baar design karo, baar-baar use karo.
  • Orchestration: pipelines kab aur kaise chalengi — scheduling, dependencies, retries.
  • Software engineering: pipelines bhi software hain — testing aur code review un par bhi lagu hota hai.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 4: Data Engineering for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous4.2 · LLM training pipeline — pretrain se fine-tune takNext →4.4 · LLMs ke liye data management pipeline
4.4Chapter 4 · Data Engineering for LLMs

LLMs ke liye data management pipeline

Generic DELC ko LLM ki needs ke hisaab se dhalne par ek specific pipeline banti hai. Isme naye sawaal aate hain jo traditional data engineering me nahi the.

LLM pipeline ke naye sawaal

  • Kaun sa data train karein? Sab data train karne layak nahi hai — copyrighted, toxic, low-quality ya biased data ko filter karna padta hai.
  • Data ko kaise chunk karein? RAG ke liye documents ko chunks me todna padta hai — chunk size aur overlap retrieval quality tay karte hain.
  • Embeddings kaise banayein aur store karein? Kaun sa embedding model use karein, vectors ko kahan store karein, index kaise banayein — ye RAG ki performance tay karta hai.
  • Data kaise update karein? Duniya badalti hai — naye documents aate hain, purane outdated hote hain. Pipeline ko incremental updates support karne chahiye, poora rebuild nahi.
  • Data lineage kaise rakhein? Agar model ne galat jawaab diya, to pata hona chahiye ki wo kis document se aaya — debugging aur compliance ke liye zaroori hai.

Event-driven vs batch updates

Batch updates: roz ya hafte me ek baar poora data refresh karo — simple, lekin stale data rehta hai. Event-driven updates: jab koi document badle, tabhi use update karo — fresh data, lekin complex pipeline. Zyadatar production systems hybrid hote hain — critical data event-driven, baaki batch.

Dynamic data management aur pruning

Data hamesha badhta hai — storage aur cost dono badhte hain. Isliye pruning zaroori hai: purana, duplicate ya irrelevant data hatao. Lekin dhyan se — jo data aaj irrelevant lage, wo kal kaam aa sakta hai. Pruning policy likho: kya hatao, kab hatao, aur kya archive karo (delete mat karo, archive karo).

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 4: Data Engineering for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous4.3 · Data Engineering Lifecycle (DELC) — 5 stagesNext →4.5 · Data sources aur types — embeddings aur vector databases
4.5Chapter 4 · Data Engineering for LLMs

Data sources aur types — embeddings aur vector databases

LLM applications me data 3 forms me hota hai: raw text, embeddings (vectors) aur structured data. Har form ka apna storage aur apna use hai.

Embeddings kya hain

Embedding text ka numeric representation hai — ek vector (numbers ki list) jisme text ka meaning encoded hota hai. Similar meaning wale texts ke vectors paas-paas hote hain. Example: "billi" aur "cat" ke vectors paas honge, "billi" aur "car" ke door. Embeddings se semantic search possible hoti hai — keyword match nahi, meaning match.

Vector databases kyun chahiye

Normal database keyword se dhoondti hai — "billi" likho to wahi word wale documents milenge. Vector database meaning se dhoondti hai — "billi" likho to cat, kitten, pet wale documents bhi milenge. RAG isi par chalta hai: user ke sawaal ka embedding banao, vector DB me sabse paas wale documents dhoondo, unhe context me model ko do.

Vector DB chunne ke criteria

  • Scale: kitne vectors honge — thousands ya billions?
  • Latency: search kitni tez chahiye — milliseconds matter karte hain?
  • Filtering: kya metadata filter chahiye — jaise "sirf 2024 ke documents"?
  • Managed vs self-hosted: managed service aasan hai, self-hosted control deta hai.
  • Cost: storage + queries — dono ka hisaab lagao.

Graph databases aur knowledge graphs

Kuch data relationships me hota hai — "X, Y ka manager hai", "A, B ka part hai". Graph database ye relationships store karta hai, aur knowledge graph se RAG aur behtar ho jata hai — sirf similar documents nahi, connected facts bhi milte hain. Example: "Is project par kaun kaam kar raha hai?" — graph se team, roles aur dependencies — sab ek saath milega.

Data types — ek jhalak

  • Structured: tables, databases — SQL se query hota hai.
  • Unstructured: documents, emails, chats — text processing chahiye.
  • Semi-structured: JSON, XML — structure bhi hai, flexibility bhi.
  • Multimodal: images, audio, video — alag encoders chahiye (Chapter 3.6).
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 4: Data Engineering for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous4.4 · LLMs ke liye data management pipelineNext →4.6 · Data quality — cleaning, dedup, decontamination, PII
4.6Chapter 4 · Data Engineering for LLMs

Data quality — cleaning, dedup, decontamination, PII

Data quality LLM ki quality hai. Kitab 5 quality practices batati hai — inme se ek bhi chhooti to model ki performance ya safety par asar padega.

1. Cleaning

Raw text me HTML tags, boilerplate, garbled characters aur formatting junk hota hai. Cleaning me ye sab hataya jata hai. Language detection bhi cleaning ka hissa hai — galat language ka text alag karo.

2. Deduplication (dedup)

Internet par wahi text baar-baar milta hai — copy-paste, mirrors, quotes. Duplicate data se model us text ko zyada weight de deta hai aur memorization badhta hai. Dedup do levels par hota hai: exact dedup (bilkul same text) aur near dedup (lagbhag same text, thoda farq). Global dedup pure dataset par hota hai — expensive lekin zaroori hai.

3. Decontamination

Test data training data me na aaye — ye decontamination hai. Agar model ne test ke sawaal pehle se dekh liye, to uska test score jhootha hoga. N-gram overlap check se contamination pakda jata hai.

4. Quality filtering

Low-quality text hatao — bahut chhota, bahut repetitive, ya bekaar content. Perplexity (model ko text kitna "surprising" lagta hai) ek signal hai — bahut high perplexity matlab text ajeeb hai, shayad kachra hai. Lekin dhyan rahe: perplexity filter se rare lekin valuable content bhi hat sakta hai.

5. PII removal aur privacy

Training data me names, emails, phone numbers, addresses ho sakte hain — model inhe memorize karke leak kar sakta hai. PII detection aur redaction zaroori hai, khaas taur par regulated industries me. Lekin PII removal perfect nahi hota — isliye privacy ek ongoing process hai, ek baar ka kaam nahi (Chapter 8).

Memorization ka khatra

Model training data ko memorize kar sakta hai — aur prompt karke use nikalwaya ja sakta hai. Dedup aur PII removal se memorization kam hoti hai, lekin khatm nahi hoti. Isi liye training data ki governance itni important hai.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 4: Data Engineering for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous4.5 · Data sources aur types — embeddings aur vector databasesNext →4.7 · Fine-tuning datasets aur dynamic data — instruction data kaise banayein
4.7Chapter 4 · Data Engineering for LLMs

Fine-tuning datasets aur dynamic data — instruction data kaise banayein

Fine-tuning ke liye chahiye instruction datasets — "instruction → response" ke pairs. Ye data pretraining data se bilkul alag hota hai: chhota, high-quality aur task-specific.

Instruction datasets ki categories

  • General instruction datasets: har tarah ke instructions — sawaal-jawaab, summarization, writing. Model ko general instruction-following sikhate hain.
  • Domain-specific instruction datasets: ek domain ke instructions — jaise medical, legal, finance. Model ko domain ki bhasha aur norms sikhate hain.
  • Task-specific datasets: ek specific kaam ke liye — jaise "support ticket ko category me dalo". Sabse chhota, sabse focused.

Instruction data banane ke tareeke

  • Human-written: experts likhte hain — sabse high quality, sabse mehenga aur slow.
  • Existing data se convert: tumhare paas jo data hai (FAQs, tickets, docs) use instruction format me badlo — sasta aur domain-accurate.
  • Automatically generate: ek bade LLM se instruction data generate karwao — tez aur sasta, lekin quality check zaroori hai. Generated data me model ki galtiyan bhi aa sakti hain — human review ya automated filters se saaf karo.
  • User interactions se: real user conversations (consent aur privacy ke saath) — sabse realistic data.

Fine-tuning data ke golden rules

  1. Quality > quantity: 1,000 achhe examples 100,000 bekaar se behtar hain.
  2. Diversity rakho: ek hi type ke examples se model narrow ho jata hai.
  3. Format consistent rakho: instruction aur response ka format har example me same ho — model pattern seekhta hai.
  4. Eval set alag rakho: training data se bilkul alag examples se test karo.
  5. Iterate karo: pehle chhota dataset, evaluate karo, phir data badhao — ek baar me sab mat dalo.

Dynamic data — data kabhi "done" nahi hota

Data badalta rehta hai: naye documents, naye user patterns, naye regulations. Isliye data pipeline ko dynamic hona chahiye — naye data ko aate hi process karo, purane ko update ya archive karo, aur model ko refresh karte raho. Event-driven updates (Chapter 4.4) iska ek tareeka hai. Aur har data change ko version karo — taaki pata chale ki model ke kis version ne kaun sa data dekha tha.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 4: Data Engineering for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous4.6 · Data quality — cleaning, dedup, decontamination, PIINext →5.1 · Training from scratch — kab aur kaise
5.1Chapter 5 · Model Domain Adaptation

Training from scratch — kab aur kaise

Training from scratch ka matlab hai: ek LLM ko zero se train karna — random weights se shuru karke, apne data par. Ye sabse powerful lekin sabse mehenga tareeka hai. Zyadatar teams ko ye karne ki zaroorat nahi padti — lekin kab zaroorat padti hai, ye samajhna important hai.

Kab training from scratch karein

  • Unique language ya domain: tumhari bhasha ya domain ke liye koi pretrained model hi nahi hai.
  • Full control chahiye: data, architecture, training — sab par control chahiye (research ya strategic reasons se).
  • Licensing: existing models ki license tumhare use case ko allow nahi karti.

Baaki sab cases me — pretrained model lo aur use adapt karo (fine-tuning, RAG, prompting). Scratch se train karna months aur millions kharch karta hai.

Training from scratch ke steps

  1. Task selection: model kya karega — ye architecture aur data dono tay karta hai.
  2. Architecture selection: encoder-only, decoder-only ya encoder-decoder — aur kitne parameters (aage section 5.2).
  3. Data preparation: massive, clean, diverse data — Chapter 4 ka poora kaam yahan aata hai.
  4. Infrastructure setup: GPUs, distributed training, checkpointing, monitoring — Chapter 9 ka kaam.
  5. Implementation: training loop, loss, optimizer, learning-rate schedule — aur bahut saara debugging.

Training ki practical mushkilein

  • Cost: compute cost hi sabse bada factor hai — isliye scaling laws samajhna zaroori hai (section 5.8).
  • Stability: badi training runs diverge kar sakti hain (loss explode ho jaye) — learning rate, initialization aur gradient clipping se control karte hain.
  • Debugging: model galat seekh raha hai ya data galat hai — ye batana mushkil hai. Isliye chhote runs se shuru karo, phir scale karo.
  • Time: ek run hafte-mahine chal sakta hai — isliye checkpointing aur resume capability must hai.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 5: Model Domain Adaptation for LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous4.7 · Fine-tuning datasets aur dynamic data — instruction data kaise banayeinNext →5.2 · LLM architectures ke three types — detail me
5.2Chapter 5 · Model Domain Adaptation

LLM architectures ke three types — detail me

Chapter 1 me architectures ka overview tha — yahan detail hai, kyunki architecture chunna training from scratch ka sabse bada decision hai.

Encoder-only (AutoEncoding) — samajhne ke liye

Model poora input ek saath padhta hai aur har word ke liye dono taraf ka context use karta hai. Masked language modeling se train hota hai — kuch words chhupao, model unhe predict kare. Best hai understanding tasks ke liye: classification, entity recognition, semantic search. Generation ke liye achha nahi hai — ye text banata nahi, text samajhta hai.

Decoder-only (AutoRegressive) — banane ke liye

Model ek ek karke agla word predict karta hai, sirf pehle wale words ko dekh kar. Causal language modeling se train hota hai. Aaj ke zyadatar LLMs isi type ke hain — GPT family, LLaMA family. Generation, chat, reasoning — sab me best hai. Limitation: ye future context nahi dekh sakta, sirf past.

Encoder-decoder (Sequence-to-sequence) — badalne ke liye

Encoder input ko samajhta hai, decoder output banata hai. Translation aur summarization jaise tasks ke liye design hua tha — ek sequence ko dusri sequence me badalna. T5 family iska example hai. Aaj kam use hota hai, kyunki decoder-only models ne in tasks me bhi achha performance dikha diya hai.

Architecture chunne ka decision tree

  • Text generate karna hai? Decoder-only.
  • Text classify/search karna hai? Encoder-only.
  • Ek sequence ko dusri me badalna hai? Encoder-decoder ya decoder-only — dono try karo.
  • Budget kam hai? Chhota decoder-only + fine-tuning — aksar sabse practical.

Naye architectures — Mamba aur aage

Transformer ke alawa bhi architectures aa rahe hain — jaise Mamba aur Mamba-2, jo attention ki jagah state-space models use karte hain aur lambi sequences par zyada efficient hain. Abhi ye experimental hain, lekin future me Transformer ko challenge kar sakte hain. Chapter 10 me inka future discuss hua hai.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 5: Model Domain Adaptation for LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous5.1 · Training from scratch — kab aur kaiseNext →5.3 · Ensembling — kai models ko ek saath chalana
5.3Chapter 5 · Model Domain Adaptation

Ensembling — kai models ko ek saath chalana

Ensembling ka matlab hai: ek model ki jagah kai models ko chalana aur unke outputs ko combine karna. Ek model galti kare to dusra sudhar de — collective wisdom.

Ensembling ke tareeke

  • Model averaging: kai models ke weights ka average lo — simple, lekin sirf tab kaam karta hai jab models similar hon.
  • Weighted ensembling: har model ko ek weight do — behtar model ko zyada weight. Weights validation data par tune hote hain.
  • Stacked ensembling: models ke outputs ko ek aur model (meta-learner) ko do, jo final decision le. Sabse powerful, sabse complex.
  • Diverse ensembles for robustness: alag-alag data ya alag architectures par train kiye models ko combine karo — diversity se robustness badhti hai.
  • Multi-step decoding aur voting: ek hi model se kai outputs generate karo (sampling), phir vote karke best chuno — self-consistency ka idea.
  • SAC technique: kitab me discuss ki gayi ek ensembling technique jo multiple samples ko combine karke reliability badhati hai.

Ensembling ke fayde aur nuksaan

FaydaNuksaan
Accuracy badhti hai — galtiyan average out hoti hainCost badhti hai — N models matlab N× compute
Robustness badhti hai — ek model fail ho to dusra sambhaleLatency badhti hai — sab models ka wait karna padta hai
Uncertainty estimate milta hai — models disagree karein to confidence low haiComplexity badhti hai — deploy aur monitor karna mushkil

Kab ensembling karein

Jab accuracy sabse important ho aur cost secondary ho — jaise medical ya financial decisions. Jab ek model se kaam na chale lekin bade model ka budget na ho — 3 chhote models ka ensemble 1 bade model se behtar aur sasta ho sakta hai. Lekin real-time apps me latency ka dhyan rakho — ensemble ko parallel chalao, sequential nahi.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 5: Model Domain Adaptation for LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous5.2 · LLM architectures ke three types — detail meNext →5.4 · Prompt engineering — model se behtar output kaise nikalein
5.4Chapter 5 · Model Domain Adaptation

Prompt engineering — model se behtar output kaise nikalein

Prompt engineering ka matlab hai: model ko aisa input dena jisse wo behtar output de — bina model ke weights badle. Ye sabse sasta aur tez adaptation tareeka hai.

Prompting ke levels

  • Zero-shot: bina example ke seedha instruction do — "Is text ko summarize karo." Simple tasks me kaam karta hai.
  • Few-shot: 2-5 examples do, phir task do. Model examples se pattern seekh kar follow karta hai. Format-sensitive tasks me bahut effective hai.
  • Chain-of-Thought (CoT): model ko "step by step socho" bolo — reasoning tasks me accuracy bahut badhti hai. Complex maths ya logic me must hai.
  • Metaprompts: prompt ke andar prompt — jaise "Tum ek expert ho, pehle plan banao, phir jawaab do." Model ko role aur process dono batate hain.

Achha prompt kaise likhein

  1. Clear aur specific raho: "achha likho" nahi, "200 words me, bullet points me, simple bhasha me likho" bolo.
  2. Context do: jo background model ko chahiye, prompt me do — model tumhare dimaag ko nahi padh sakta.
  3. Format batao: output kis format me chahiye — JSON, table, bullets? Format batane se parsing aasan hoti hai.
  4. Constraints lagao: kya nahi karna hai — "personal data mat likho", "sirf diye gaye documents se jawaab do".
  5. Iterate karo: pehla prompt kabhi perfect nahi hota — test karo, output dekho, prompt sudharo. Prompt ko code ki tarah version karo.

Prompt engineering ki limits

Prompt se tum model ko context de sakte ho, lekin uska behavior nahi badal sakte. Agar model ko ek specific format hamesha follow karna hai, ya ek style me likhna hai, to prompt se kaam chal sakta hai — lekin agar behavior deep change chahiye, to fine-tuning behtar hai (aage section 5.8 me comparison hai). Aur lamba prompt har request par cost badhata hai — prompt engineering ek "mortgage" hai, fine-tuning ek "upfront payment" (Chapter 5 me kitab ki analogy).

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 5: Model Domain Adaptation for LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous5.3 · Ensembling — kai models ko ek saath chalanaNext →5.5 · RAG — retrieval-augmented generation, detail me
5.5Chapter 5 · Model Domain Adaptation

RAG — retrieval-augmented generation, detail me

RAG ka idea simple hai: model ko jawaab dene se pehle tumhare documents se relevant information dhoond kar do. Isse model tumhara data use karta hai, hallucination kam hoti hai, aur jawaab verifiable hota hai.

RAG pipeline ke steps

  1. Documents load karo: PDFs, docs, web pages, databases — sab sources se.
  2. Chunk karo: documents ko chhote chunks me todo (jaise 500-1000 characters) — overlap rakho taaki context na toote.
  3. Embed karo: har chunk ka embedding banao — ek vector jo uska meaning capture karta hai.
  4. Index karo: embeddings ko vector database me store karo — fast search ke liye.
  5. Retrieve karo: user ke sawaal ka embedding banao, vector DB se top-k similar chunks dhoondo.
  6. Rerank karo: retrieved chunks ko relevance ke hisaab se dobara rank karo — behtar chunks upar aayein.
  7. Generate karo: sawaal + retrieved chunks ko model ko do — model inhi ke basis par jawaab de.

RAG ko behtar kaise banayein

  • Chunking strategy: chunk size matter karta hai — bahut chhota chunk context khota hai, bahut bada chunk irrelevant info lata hai. Apne documents par experiment karo.
  • Embedding model: domain ke hisaab se embedding model chuno — generic embeddings har domain me achhe nahi hote.
  • Hybrid search: keyword search (BM25) + vector search — dono ko combine karo, kyunki kabhi keyword exact match chahiye, kabhi meaning match.
  • Reranking: ek cross-encoder reranker retrieval quality ko bahut badha deta hai — thoda latency badhta hai, lekin worth hai.
  • Query rewriting: user ka vague sawaal clear karo — pehle sawaal ko rewrite karo, phir retrieve karo.

Graph RAG — aage ka step

Normal RAG documents retrieve karta hai; Graph RAG knowledge graph se connected facts bhi retrieve karta hai — entities aur unke relationships. Complex sawaalon ke liye (jaise "Is project ke stakeholders kaun hain aur unke beech kya dependencies hain?") Graph RAG behtar hai. Lekin graph banana aur maintain karna extra kaam hai.

RAG ki limits

RAG model ko knowledge deta hai, lekin uska behavior nahi badalta. Agar model ko ek specific style ya format me hamesha jawaab dena hai, to RAG se nahi hoga — fine-tuning chahiye. Aur RAG sirf utna achha hai jitni retrieval achhi hai — garbage retrieval matlab garbage jawaab.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 5: Model Domain Adaptation for LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous5.4 · Prompt engineering — model se behtar output kaise nikaleinNext →5.6 · Fine-tuning — model ko apne domain me dhalna
5.6Chapter 5 · Model Domain Adaptation

Fine-tuning — model ko apne domain me dhalna

Fine-tuning ka matlab hai: pretrained model ko apne data par aur train karna, taaki wo tumhare domain, task ya style me behtar ho jaye. Ye model ke weights badalta hai — isliye ye prompt engineering se deeper change hai.

Fine-tuning ke types

  • Full fine-tuning: model ke saare parameters update karo — sabse powerful, sabse mehenga, sabse zyada data chahiye.
  • Adaptive fine-tuning: model ko naye domain ke data par adapt karo — domain ki bhasha aur facts sikhane ke liye.
  • Behavioral fine-tuning: model ka behavior badlo — jaise hamesha ek specific format me jawaab de, ya ek specific tone me baat kare.
  • Instruction tuning: instruction-response pairs par train karo — model instructions follow karna seekhta hai.
  • RLHF fine-tuning: human preferences se align karo — helpful, honest, harmless (Chapter 1.4 me overview tha).
  • Multimodal fine-tuning: text ke saath images ya audio par bhi fine-tune karo — multimodal models ke liye.

Fine-tuning ka process

  1. Data taiyaar karo: instruction datasets — Chapter 4.7 ka kaam. Quality sabse important hai.
  2. Base model chuno: tumhare task aur budget ke hisaab se — chhota model bhi fine-tune karke bade se behtar ho sakta hai.
  3. Hyperparameters set karo: learning rate, epochs, batch size — chhota learning rate, kam epochs se shuru karo.
  4. Train karo aur evaluate karo: har epoch ke baad eval set par test karo — overfitting dikhte hi roko (early stopping).
  5. Deploy karo aur monitor karo: production me performance dekho — drift aaye to dobara fine-tune karo.

Fine-tuning ke risks

  • Catastrophic forgetting: model naya seekhte hue purana bhool jaye. Example kitab me: ek model jo blog posts likhta tha, use product chat data par fine-tune kiya gaya — uske baad wo blog post likhne ko kahe to "I'm too busy" jawaab dene laga. Fine-tuning ne uska behavior badal diya tha.
  • Overfitting: chhote data par zyada train karo to model data rat le, generalize na kare.
  • Cost: full fine-tuning mehenga hai — GPT-4o ki fine-tuning cost kitab ke likhte waqt $25,000 per million tokens thi.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 5: Model Domain Adaptation for LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous5.5 · RAG — retrieval-augmented generation, detail meNext →5.7 · PEFT — parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA aur aage)
5.7Chapter 5 · Model Domain Adaptation

PEFT — parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA aur aage)

Full fine-tuning me billions of parameters update hote hain — mehenga aur slow. PEFT ka idea hai: model ke zyadatar parameters ko freeze karke, sirf ek chhota sa hissa train karo. Result lagbhag same, cost bahut kam.

LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) — sabse popular PEFT

LoRA model ke weight matrices ke saath chhote "adapter" matrices jodta hai — sirf ye adapters train hote hain, original weights freeze rehte hain. Ek 7B model ko fine-tune karne ke liye sirf kuch million parameters train karne padte hain — GPU memory aur time dono bahut kam lagte hain. Aur adapters ko alag se save karke switch kar sakte ho — ek base model, kai tasks ke adapters.

PEFT ke aur tareeke

  • Adapters: model ke layers ke beech chhote neural networks insert karo — sirf wahi train hon.
  • Prefix tuning: input ke aage trainable "prefix" vectors jodo — model unhe dekh kar apna behavior badalta hai.
  • Prompt tuning: prefix tuning jaisa, lekin soft prompts embeddings level par kaam karte hain.
  • Instruction tuning (PEFT style): adapters ke saath instruction data par train karo — kam data me instruction following.

PEFT vs full fine-tuning

AspectFull fine-tuningPEFT (LoRA)
Trainable parametersSab (billions)0.1–1% (millions)
GPU memoryBahut zyadaKam — single GPU par bhi possible
QualitySabse achhi (usually)Lagbhag same — zyadatar tasks me
Catastrophic forgettingZyada riskKam risk — base model freeze rehta hai
Multi-taskHar task ke liye alag model copyEk base + kai adapters — switch karna aasan

Practical rule: pehle LoRA try karo — agar quality kaafi ho to full fine-tuning ki zaroorat hi nahi. Full fine-tuning tab jab LoRA se kaam na chale ya domain bahut alag ho.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 5: Model Domain Adaptation for LLM-Based Applications. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous5.6 · Fine-tuning — model ko apne domain me dhalnaNext →5.8 · Fine-tuning vs prompt engineering, MoE aur optimization ke lessons
5.8Chapter 5 · Model Domain Adaptation

Fine-tuning vs prompt engineering, MoE aur optimization ke lessons

Ye section Chapter 5 ka sabse practical hissa hai: kab kya chunna hai, MoE kya hai, aur model optimization ke wo lessons jo har LLMOps engineer ko pata hone chahiye.

Fine-tuning vs prompt engineering — faisla kaise karein

Prompt engineering model ko context deti hai — wo kya jaanta hai. Fine-tuning model ka behavior badalti hai — wo kaise kaam karta hai. Upar wali figure yahi quadrant dikhati hai.

  • Cost: fine-tuning upfront mehenga hai (compute cost), prompt engineering har request par mehenga hai (lamba prompt = zyada tokens). Kitab ki analogy: fine-tuning ek upfront payment hai, prompt engineering ek mortgage hai.
  • Model lifespan: agar model 2 saal me badal jayega, to 10 saal ke liye prepay karna bewakoofi hai — prompt engineering behtar hai.
  • Example: model ko specific XML format me output chahiye, jo dusre system ko consume karna hai — fine-tuning yahan prompt se behtar hai, kyunki format behavior hai, knowledge nahi.
  • Rule: dono available hon to pehle prompt engineering try karo — kuch ghanton me pata chal jayega. Fine-tuning tab jab prompt se kaam na chale.

Mixture of Experts (MoE)

MoE me ek bade model ke andar kai chhote "expert" sub-networks hote hain. Har input ke liye ek gating network tay karta hai ki kaun se 1-2 experts kaam karein — baaki soye rehte hain. Isse model trillions of parameters ka ho sakta hai, lekin har query par sirf ek chhota hissa chalta hai — compute cost low rehti hai.

  • GShard: top-2 experts choose karta hai — zyada expressive, lekin communication overhead zyada.
  • Switch Transformer: top-1 expert (hard routing) — kam communication, kam memory.
  • Load balancing: sabse badi challenge — gating sab kaam kuch experts ko de de to baaki waste hote hain. Isliye training me load-balancing loss add kiya jata hai.
  • Expert capacity: har expert ek limit tak tokens handle kar sakta hai — zyada tokens aaye to drop ya reroute hote hain.

Resource-constrained devices ke liye optimization

  • Prompt caching: frequently aane wale prompts ke results cache karo — dobara compute mat karo.
  • KV caching: attention ke key-value tensors cache karo — sequential generation tez hoti hai.
  • Quantization: weights ko 32-bit se 8-bit ya 4-bit me badlo — memory aur speed dono behtar, accuracy me halki girawat. Static, dynamic aur quantization-aware training (QAT) — 3 types hain.
  • Pruning: bekaar weights, neurons ya layers hatao — structured (poore neurons) ya unstructured (individual weights).
  • Distillation: bade "teacher" model se chhote "student" model ko sikhao — student teacher jaisa behave kare, lekin chhota aur tez ho.

Lessons — scaling laws, Chinchilla, learning rate

  • Scaling laws: performance model size, data aur compute ke saath predictable curve par badhti hai — lekin diminishing returns aate hain. Model size aur data dono ko ek saath double karna, sirf ek ko double karne se behtar hai.
  • Chinchilla approach: model ko bada karne ki jagah, fixed size par zyada data se train karo — fixed compute budget me chhota model + zyada data, bade model + kam data se behtar perform karta hai. Kitab ka example: fixed "medium" model, data 4x badhao.
  • Learning-rate optimization: shuru me learning rate dheere badhao (warmup), phir smoothly ghatao (cosine decay) — isse convergence stable aur behtar hoti hai.
  • Speculative sampling: chhote model se draft generate karo, bade model se verify karo — generation tez hoti hai.
  • Overtraining se bacho: zyada train karna bhi nuksaan karta hai — eval par nazar rakho, early stopping use karo.
# Scaling law — illustrative (kitab ke Example 5-11 jaisa)
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
model_sizes = np.logspace(1, 4, 100)  # 10^1 se 10^4 tak
performance = np.log(model_sizes) / np.log(10)
plt.plot(model_sizes, performance, label="Scaling Law")
plt.xscale("log")
plt.xlabel("Model Size (log scale)")
plt.ylabel("Performance")
plt.title("Scaling Law for LLMs")
plt.legend()
plt.show()

# Chinchilla approach — illustrative (kitab ke Example 5-12 jaisa)
model_size = "medium"          # model size fixed rakho
data_multiplier = 4            # dataset 4x badhao
model = load_model(size=model_size)
dataset = augment_dataset(original_dataset, multiplier=data_multiplier)
train_model(model, dataset)
evaluate_model(model)

6.1Chapter 6 · API-First LLM Deployment

API-first approach — LLM ko service ki tarah deploy karo

API-first ka matlab hai: LLM application ko ek API ke roop me design karo — pehle API contract tay karo, phir uske peeche ka implementation banao. Isse tumhari application kisi bhi client se jud sakti hai — web, mobile, ya dusri services.

LLM APIs ke 3 types

  • LLM model APIs: seedha model ko call karo — prompt bhejo, completion lo. Sabse simple, sabse direct.
  • LLM platform APIs: platform ke through model use karo — saath me tools, monitoring, safety features bhi milte hain.
  • LLMs-as-APIs: apna khud ka model host karke use API bana do — full control, tumhari infrastructure.

API-first kyun

  • Decoupling: frontend aur model alag ho jate hain — model badlo, frontend ko pata bhi nahi chalega.
  • Reusability: ek API ko kai applications use kar sakti hain — web app, mobile app, internal tools.
  • Scalability: API ko independently scale karo — model ke peeche replicas badhao, frontend ko chhedo mat.
  • Testing: API contract par test likhna aasan hai — model ke behavior ko API level par verify karo.

API design ke principles

  • RESTful ya clear contract: endpoints, request/response format, error codes — sab document hone chahiye.
  • Streaming support: LLM response token-by-token aaye — user ko pehla token jaldi dikhao, poora jawaab ka wait mat karwao.
  • Versioning: API ka version rakho (v1, v2) — naya version aaye to purana turant mat todo (Chapter 6 me API versioning aur lifecycle management detail me hai).
  • Auth aur rate limiting: kaun call kar sakta hai, kitni baar — abuse aur cost control ke liye zaroori hai.
# FastAPI se LLM API — kitab ke example jaisa (illustrative)
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/generate")
def generate(prompt: str):
    # yahan model call hoga — prompt -> completion
    return {"response": "model ka jawaab yahan aayega"}

# Server chalao: python app.py — phir POST /generate par prompt bhejo
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 6: API-First LLM Deployment. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous5.8 · Fine-tuning vs prompt engineering, MoE aur optimization ke lessonsNext →6.2 · Deployment workflow — containerization se orchestration tak
6.2Chapter 6 · API-First LLM Deployment

Deployment workflow — containerization se orchestration tak

LLM ko production me deploy karna ek workflow hai — 5 steps, har ek me apne tools aur apne checks. Kitab is workflow ko step-by-step batati hai.

Deployment workflow ke 5 steps

  1. Containerization: application aur uski dependencies ko Docker container me band karo — "mere machine par chalta hai" se "har machine par chalta hai" tak.
  2. Environment setup: dev, staging, production — teeno environments same hone chahiye. Secrets aur configs ko code se alag rakho.
  3. Orchestration: containers ko manage karo — Kubernetes ya Docker Swarm se replicas, scaling aur health checks.
  4. Pipeline automation: CI/CD se deploy automate karo — har commit par test, har release par staged rollout.
  5. Monitoring setup: deploy ke saath monitoring bhi jaye — latency, errors, cost, quality — bina monitoring ke deploy andha hai.

Docker — LLM deployment ka standard

Dockerfile me likho: base image (Python + CUDA), dependencies install karo, model files copy karo, API server start karo. Ek baar image ban jaye, wo kahin bhi chalegi — laptop, server, cloud.

# Dockerfile — illustrative (LLM API ke liye)
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY app.py .
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["python", "app.py"]

Kubernetes vs Docker Swarm

AspectDocker SwarmKubernetes
ComplexitySimple, jaldi setupComplex, seekhne me time
ScalingBasicAdvanced — auto-scaling, rolling updates
Multi-modelChhote setups ke liye theekBade setups ke liye behtar
EcosystemChhotaBada — monitoring, service mesh, sab kuch

Chhote project se shuru karo to Swarm kaafi hai; production scale par Kubernetes standard hai. Kitab Kubernetes ko multi-model deployment ke liye recommend karti hai.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 6: API-First LLM Deployment. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
