6.3Chapter 6 · API-First LLM Deployment

API design — versioning, rate limiting, auth aur streaming

Ek achhi LLM API sirf "kaam karti" nahi hai — wo secure, fair aur future-proof bhi hoti hai. Is section me API design ke 4 pillars hain.

1. API versioning aur lifecycle management

API badlegi — naya model, naya format, naye features. Versioning se purane clients nahi toot te: /v1/generate chalta rahe, /v2/generate naya aaye. Har version ka lifecycle hota hai: active → deprecated (naye users ko mana karo) → sunset (band karo, pehle se notice dekar). Model version aur API version — dono ko track karo, kyunki model update se behavior badal sakta hai.

2. Rate limiting — abuse aur cost control

Rate limiting batata hai ki ek user kitne requests kar sakta hai — jaise 100 requests per minute. Isse hota hai: DoS attacks rokte hain, ek user dusre ka resource nahi khata, aur cost control me rehti hai. Implement karne ke tareeke: token bucket, fixed window, sliding window. Rate limit cross ho to 429 error do — clear message ke saath ki kab retry karein.

3. Authentication aur authorization

  • API keys: simple, har client ko ek key — revoke karna aasan hai.
  • OAuth / JWT: user-level auth — kaun hai, use kya karne ki permission hai.
  • Least privilege: har key ko sirf utni permission do jitni zaroori hai — ek read-only key se model retrain nahi hona chahiye.

4. Streaming — user experience ka sawaal

LLM response aane me seconds lagte hain. Agar user ko poora jawaab ek saath dikhao, to wo wait karta hai. Streaming me tokens aate hi dikhte hain — user ko lagta hai model "bol raha hai". Implement karne ke liye Server-Sent Events (SSE) ya WebSockets use hote hain. Streaming se time-to-first-token kam dikhta hai, jo user satisfaction ka sabse bada factor hai.

Error handling aur timeouts

  • Timeouts set karo: model hang ho to request hamesha latki na rahe — sensible timeout (jaise 60s) rakho.
  • Retry with backoff: transient failures par retry karo — lekin exponential backoff ke saath, taaki system ko aur load na do.
  • Clear errors: 400 (galat request), 401 (auth fail), 429 (rate limit), 500 (server error), 503 (overloaded) — sahi code, sahi message.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 6: API-First LLM Deployment. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous6.2 · Deployment workflow — containerization se orchestration takNext →6.4 · RAG optimization in deployment — retriever se reranker tak
6.4Chapter 6 · API-First LLM Deployment

RAG optimization in deployment — retriever se reranker tak

RAG ko deploy karna sirf "vector DB lagao" nahi hai — retrieval quality, latency aur cost ka balance hai. Kitab RAG optimization ke 4 levers batati hai.

Lever 1 — Retriever tuning

Retriever wo component hai jo relevant chunks dhoondta hai. Ise tune karo: top-k kitna ho (5? 10? 20?) — zyada chunks matlab zyada context, lekin zyada noise aur cost bhi. Embedding model domain ke hisaab se chuno. Hybrid search (keyword + vector) se recall badhta hai.

Lever 2 — Reranking

Retriever ke top-k results ko ek reranker se dobara rank karo — cross-encoder reranker relevance ko behtar pakadta hai. Cost: ek extra model call. Fayda: top-3 chunks ki quality bahut badhti hai, jisse generation behtar hota hai aur tokens bachte hain.

Lever 3 — Caching

  • Embedding caching: same text ka embedding dobara mat banao — cache me rakho.
  • Prompt caching: frequently aane wale prompts ke results cache karo — customer support me same sawaal baar-baar aate hain.
  • Semantic caching: similar meaning wale sawaalon ke cached jawaab do — exact match ki zaroorat nahi.

Lever 4 — Chunking aur index optimization

Chunk size, overlap aur index type (HNSW, IVF) — teeno retrieval quality aur speed ko affect karte hain. Apne documents par experiment karo: 3-4 chunking strategies try karo, eval set par measure karo, best chuno. Ye ek baar ka kaam nahi — documents badalte hain to chunking bhi review karni chahiye.

RAG optimization ka order: pehle retrieval quality (eval se measure karo), phir latency (caching, reranking budget), phir cost (chhota model, kam tokens). Quality se compromise karke cost bachana aksar mehenga padta hai — galat jawaab ka cost, token cost se zyada hota hai.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 6: API-First LLM Deployment. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous6.3 · API design — versioning, rate limiting, auth aur streamingNext →6.5 · Latency optimization — KV cache, batching, Triton
6.5Chapter 6 · API-First LLM Deployment

Latency optimization — KV cache, batching, Triton

LLM inference slow kyun hota hai, aur use tez kaise karein? Latency optimization ke 5 tareeke hain — har ek ka apna trade-off hai.

1. KV caching

Transformer har naye token ke liye pehle ke tokens ke key-value tensors dobara compute karta hai — wasteful. KV caching me ye tensors save karke reuse kiye jate hain — generation 2-5x tez ho sakti hai. Cost: memory — lambi conversations me cache bada hota hai. Paged attention (Chapter 9) is memory ko efficiently manage karta hai.

2. Dynamic batching

Ek ek request alag se process karne ki jagah, kai requests ko ek batch me process karo — GPU utilization badhta hai, per-request cost ghatti hai. Trade-off: batch bharne ke liye thoda wait karna padta hai — latency thodi badh sakti hai. Continuous batching (jaise vLLM me) is trade-off ko aur behtar banata hai.

3. Quantization (inference par)

Model ke weights ko 16-bit ya 8-bit me chalao — memory kam, speed zyada. Accuracy me halki girawat aati hai, lekin zyadatar tasks me negligible hoti hai. 4-bit quantization se model chhote GPUs par bhi chal sakta hai.

4. Model serving frameworks — Triton aur aage

NVIDIA Triton Inference Server production serving ka standard hai — dynamic batching, multi-model serving, GPU utilization — sab built-in. Iske alawa vLLM, TensorRT-LLM jaise LLM-specific servers hain jo paged attention aur continuous batching se throughput ko bahut badha dete hain.

5. Speculative decoding

Chhota, tez model draft tokens generate kare, bada model unhe verify kare — galat draft ko correct kare. Isse generation 2-3x tez ho sakti hai bina quality khoye.

Latency measure kaise karein

  • Time to first token (TTFT): user ko pehla word kitni der me dikha — streaming UX ke liye sabse important.
  • Inter-token latency: tokens ke beech ka gap — reading experience ke liye important.
  • Total latency: poora jawaab kitni der me aaya.
  • p95/p99: average nahi, percentiles dekho — 1% slow requests hi user complaints banate hain.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 6: API-First LLM Deployment. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous6.4 · RAG optimization in deployment — retriever se reranker takNext →6.6 · Multi-model orchestration aur scaling — ek se zyada models chalana
6.6Chapter 6 · API-First LLM Deployment

Multi-model orchestration aur scaling — ek se zyada models chalana

Production me aksar ek model kaafi nahi hota — alag tasks ke liye alag models, ya ek hi task ke liye kai models (champion-challenger). Multi-model orchestration inhe ek saath chalane ka tareeka hai.

Multi-model kyun

  • Alag tasks, alag models: classification ke liye chhota model, generation ke liye bada model, embeddings ke liye teesra model.
  • Cost optimization: simple sawaal chhote (saste) model ko, mushkil sawaal bade model ko — router decide kare (cascade pattern).
  • A/B testing: naya model purane ke saath shadow me chalao — compare karo, phir switch karo.
  • Fallback: ek model fail ho to dusra sambhale — reliability badhti hai.

Orchestration patterns

  • Router: request ko dekh kar decide karo ki kaun sa model handle kare — complexity, cost ya task type ke basis par.
  • Cascade: pehle chhota model try karo — confidence low ho to bade model ko bhejo.
  • Ensemble: kai models ko chalao, outputs combine karo (Chapter 5.3).
  • Pipeline: models ko sequence me chalao — pehla model retrieve kare, dusra generate kare, teesra verify kare.

Scaling — replicas aur load balancing

Load badhe to model ke replicas badhao — Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler se automatically. Load balancer requests ko replicas me baante. Dhyan do: LLM replicas stateless hone chahiye — session state bahar (Redis ya database) me rakho, taaki koi bhi replica kisi bhi request ko handle kar sake.

Multi-model deployment ki challenges

  • GPU sharing: kai models ek GPU par chalane se memory contention hoti hai — model offloading ya alag GPUs ka faisla karna padta hai.
  • Version management: har model ka apna version, apna config — sab track karna padta hai.
  • Monitoring complexity: har model ke alag metrics — ek unified dashboard chahiye.
  • Cost: idle models bhi GPU khate hain — scale-to-zero (jab use na ho to band karo) se bachao, lekin cold start ka dhyan rakho.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 6: API-First LLM Deployment. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous6.5 · Latency optimization — KV cache, batching, TritonNext →7.1 · LLM evaluation mushkil kyun hai
7.1Chapter 7 · Evaluation for LLMs

LLM evaluation mushkil kyun hai

Traditional ML me evaluation aasan thi — accuracy nikalo, ho gaya. LLM me "sahi jawaab" ek nahi hota, isliye evaluation ek research problem ban gayi hai. Ye chapter batata hai ki evaluation mushkil kyun hai aur use kaise karna hai.

Evaluation mushkil kyun hai — 5 reasons

  • Ek sawaal, kai sahi jawaab: "Paris kya hai?" ka jawaab "France ki rajdhani" bhi sahi hai aur "Ek shahar jo Seine nadi par hai" bhi. Dono ko kaise score karein?
  • Non-deterministic output: same prompt par bhi output alag ho sakta hai — ek baar ka test kaafi nahi, kai baar chalana padta hai.
  • Subjective quality: "achha essay" kya hai — ye measure karna mushkil hai. Fluency, coherence, factuality — sab alag dimensions hain.
  • Hallucination: model confident hokar galat bol sakta hai — aur galat jawaab fluent bhi ho sakta hai, isliye pakadna mushkil hai.
  • Cost: achhi evaluation me human review ya bade LLM judges chahiye — dono mehenga hai.

Traditional ML vs LLM evaluation

Upar wali figure dikhati hai ki traditional ML me evaluation reactive thi — model fail ho to pata chalta tha. LLM me evaluation proactive honi chahiye — deploy se pehle, deploy ke baad continuous, har change par. Kyunki LLM ka behavior unpredictable hai, isliye evaluation ek baar ka kaam nahi, ek ongoing process hai.

Evaluation ka framework — 3 layers

  1. Offline evaluation: deploy se pehle — benchmarks, apna eval set, human review.
  2. Online evaluation: production me — real user interactions par metrics, feedback, A/B tests.
  3. Continuous evaluation: har model/prompt/data change par eval dobara chalao — regression pakdo.
Golden rule: bina eval set ke LLM deploy mat karo. Eval set tumhara safety net hai — har change se pehle use chalao, aur agar score gire to deploy roko.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 7: Evaluation for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous6.6 · Multi-model orchestration aur scaling — ek se zyada models chalanaNext →7.2 · Evaluation metrics — n-gram se LLM-judge tak
7.2Chapter 7 · Evaluation for LLMs

Evaluation metrics — n-gram se LLM-judge tak

LLM metrics 3 families me batte hain: n-gram based (text overlap), similarity based (meaning overlap) aur LLM based (dusra LLM judge kare). Har family ki apni strength aur weakness hai.

1. N-gram based metrics — text overlap

Ye metrics generated text aur expected answer ke beech n words ke sequences (n-grams) ka overlap dekhte hain. BLEU machine translation ke liye use hota hai, ROUGE summarization ke liye. Example: expected answer "Paris" hai aur model bole "Paris" to 100% match; lekin model bole "The capital of France is Paris" to sirf 16.6% words match karenge — jabki jawaab sahi hai. Isi liye n-gram metrics short, exact answers par achhe hain, lambi creative generation par nahi.

2. Similarity based metrics — meaning overlap

Ye embeddings se poore sentences ki similarity nikalte hain:

  • BERTScore: content overlap aur fluency — dono measure karta hai.
  • SemScore: check karta hai ki generated text wahi meaning aur intent convey kar raha hai ya nahi.
  • MoverScore: ek text ko dusre me badalne ke liye kitni "mehnat" lagegi — kam mehnat matlab zyada similar.

Problem: "Teh KaPiTaLL of Franceland is PARIS" — spelling galat hai, "Franceland" word hi nahi hai — lekin meaning similar hone se score high aayega. Isliye similarity metrics akeli kaafi nahi hain.

3. LLM based metrics — LLM judge kare

Ek LLM (judge) dusre LLM ke output ko score karta hai — coherence, fluency, factual consistency par. Popular metrics:

  • G-Eval: generated text ko coherence, fluency aur factual consistency par score karta hai — ek LLM judge ke through.
  • UniEval: fluency, grammaticality aur factual coherence — kai factors ko ensemble of LLM evaluators se dekhta hai.
  • GPTScore: ek LLM se generation quality ko score karwata hai.

LLM judges expensive hote hain aur unme bhi bias ho sakta hai — judge apne jaise outputs ko zyada score de sakta hai. Isliye LLM metrics ko human spot-checks ke saath use karo.

Kaun sa metric kab

TaskBest metrics
Classification / extractionPrecision, recall, F1, accuracy
TranslationBLEU + human review
SummarizationROUGE + BERTScore + human review
Open-ended generationLLM judge + human review
RAGRetrieval metrics (hit rate, MRR) + generation metrics
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 7: Evaluation for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous7.1 · LLM evaluation mushkil kyun haiNext →7.3 · Benchmarks — GLUE, MMLU, HellaSwag aur aage
7.3Chapter 7 · Evaluation for LLMs

Benchmarks — GLUE, MMLU, HellaSwag aur aage

Benchmarks standard test sets hain jinse alag models ko compare kiya jata hai. Lekin benchmarks ko samajh kar use karna zaroori hai — ek benchmark score poori kahani nahi batata.

Popular benchmarks

  • GLUE: General Language Understanding Evaluation — natural language understanding tasks ka suite (sentiment, inference, similarity). Classic benchmark, aaj saturated ho gaya hai.
  • MMLU: Massive Multitask Language Understanding — 57 subjects me multiple-choice questions (maths, history, law, science). Model ki broad knowledge naapta hai.
  • HellaSwag: commonsense reasoning — sentence complete karo, sabse sensible option chuno.
  • HumanEval: code generation — function likho, tests pass karo.
  • TruthfulQA: model sach bolta hai ya common misconceptions repeat karta hai — hallucination naapne ke liye.
  • BBH (Big-Bench Hard): mushkil reasoning tasks — jo models ke liye challenging hain.

Benchmarks ki limits — dhyan se padho

  • Saturation: top models kai benchmarks par human-level ya usse upar pahunch gaye hain — benchmark ab differentiate nahi karta.
  • Contamination: benchmark data training data me leak ho sakta hai — score inflated ho jata hai.
  • Narrow scope: benchmark ek task naapta hai, tumhara real use case alag ho sakta hai. MMLU par 90% score ka matlab tumhare support tickets par 90% accuracy nahi hai.
  • Gaming: models ko benchmark par optimize kiya ja sakta hai bina real capability badhe.

Apna benchmark banao — sabse important

Public benchmarks se model shortlist karo, lekin final decision apne eval set par lo: 50-100 real examples, apne users ke, apne domain ke. Ye eval set tumhara sabse valuable asset hai — use version karo, use har change par chalao, aur use kabhi training data me mat milao.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 7: Evaluation for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous7.2 · Evaluation metrics — n-gram se LLM-judge takNext →7.4 · RAG evaluation — retrieval aur generation dono naapo
7.4Chapter 7 · Evaluation for LLMs

RAG evaluation — retrieval aur generation dono naapo

RAG ki evaluation do hisson me hoti hai: retrieval sahi hua ya nahi, aur generation sahi hua ya nahi. Dono me se ek bhi kharab ho to final jawaab kharab hoga.

Retrieval metrics

  • Hit rate (top-k accuracy): kitni baar sahi document top-k results me aaya? k=5 par 80% hit rate matlab 100 me se 80 baar sahi doc top-5 me tha.
  • MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank): pehla sahi result kis rank par aaya — rank 1 par aaye to score 1, rank 2 par 0.5, rank 3 par 0.33. Average lo.
  • MAP (Mean Average Precision): ranking ki overall quality — sahi docs upar aaye ya neeche?
  • Recall: kitne relevant documents retrieve hue, total relevant me se?
  • Precision: retrieved documents me se kitne relevant the?

Generation metrics (RAG context me)

  • Faithfulness: jawaab retrieved context se support hota hai ya model ne invent kiya? Ye RAG ka sabse important metric hai — hallucination yahi pakdi jati hai.
  • Answer relevance: jawaab sawaal se relevant hai ya bhatak gaya?
  • Context precision: retrieved chunks me se kitne jawaab ke liye useful the?
  • Context recall: jawaab ke liye zaroori information retrieved chunks me thi ya nahi?

RAG evaluation ka practical process

  1. Eval set banao: sawaal + expected answer + kaun se documents relevant hain — teeno likho. Ye mehnat wala kaam hai, lekin bina iske RAG tuning andha hai.
  2. Retrieval ko pehle tune karo: generation se pehle retrieval ko achha banao — chunking, embedding, top-k, reranking — sab yahan tune hote hain.
  3. Phir generation ko evaluate karo: faithfulness aur relevance dekho — LLM judge ya human review se.
  4. End-to-end test karo: final jawaab user ke liye useful hai ya nahi — yehi asli metric hai.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 7: Evaluation for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous7.3 · Benchmarks — GLUE, MMLU, HellaSwag aur aageNext →7.5 · Agentic systems ki evaluation — agents ko kaise test karein
7.5Chapter 7 · Evaluation for LLMs

Agentic systems ki evaluation — agents ko kaise test karein

Agents ki evaluation sabse mushkil hai — kyunki agent ek jawaab nahi deta, ek process chalata hai. Sahi final answer bhi galat process se aa sakta hai, aur sahi process bhi kabhi-kabhi galat answer de sakta hai.

Agent evaluation ke dimensions

  • Task success rate: kitne tasks poore hue — final outcome sahi tha ya nahi? Ye sabse basic metric hai.
  • Step efficiency: task kitne steps me hua — kam steps matlab behtar planning. Zyada steps matlab bhatakna ya retry.
  • Tool use accuracy: agent ne sahi tool chuna ya nahi? Galat tool matlab galat rasta.
  • Tool call success: tool calls me se kitne succeed hue — errors kitne aaye?
  • Cost per task: ek task me kitne tokens aur kitne LLM calls lage — agents me ye jaldi badhta hai.
  • Recovery: jab step fail ho, to agent recover kar pata hai ya atak jata hai?

Agent evaluation ki khaas mushkilein

  • Non-determinism: same task dobara chalao to alag trajectory mil sakti hai — ek run ka result kaafi nahi, kai runs ka average lo.
  • Partial credit: agent ne 10 me se 8 steps sahi kiye — use 0 ya 1 score do? Step-level scoring chahiye.
  • Long tasks: lambi tasks evaluate karna mehenga hai — har step LLM calls khata hai.
  • Human judgment: kai agent outputs ko sirf human hi judge kar sakta hai — automated metrics kaafi nahi hain.

Practical approach — traces aur rubrics

Har agent run ki trace save karo — kaun se steps, kaun se tool calls, kya observations. Phir traces ko rubric se score karo — jaise "sahi tools use hue? (0-2), plan logical tha? (0-2), final answer sahi tha? (0-2)". Rubric-based scoring se tumhe pata chalega ki agent kahan fail ho raha hai — planning me, tool use me, ya final answer me.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 7: Evaluation for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous7.4 · RAG evaluation — retrieval aur generation dono naapoNext →7.6 · Logging aur observability — LLM system ke andar kya ho raha hai
7.6Chapter 7 · Evaluation for LLMs

Logging aur observability — LLM system ke andar kya ho raha hai

Observability ka matlab hai: production system ke andar kya ho raha hai, ye dekh paana. LLM systems me ye aur bhi zaroori hai — kyunki model ka behavior unpredictable hai, aur bina logs ke tum andhe ho.

Logging styles — event se session tak

Upar wali figure dikhati hai ki logging isolated events se full sessions tak ja sakti hai. Event-level logs: ek request, ek response — simple, lekin context nahi milta. Session-level logs: poori conversation, saare tool calls, saare steps — detailed, lekin heavy. Detailed session logs se patterns dhoondhna aasan hota hai — jaise "users is step par atak rahe hain" ya "ye prompt hamesha galat output deta hai". Production me session-level logging rakho, lekin PII ko mask karke.

RAG workflow me kya log karein

Upar wali figure RAG application ka workflow dikhati hai — har step log karne layak hai: user query, retrieved chunks (kaun se, kitne), reranked order, prompt, model response, latency, tokens, cost. Agar jawaab galat aaye to tumhe pata chalna chahiye ki problem retrieval me thi ya generation me — bina step-level logs ke ye impossible hai.

Observability pipeline

Upar wali figure LLMs ke liye observability pipeline dikhati hai — logs, metrics aur traces ko collect karke dashboards aur alerts me badalna. Pipeline me hota hai: collection (har component se data lo), processing (PII mask karo, enrich karo), storage (searchable rakho), visualization (Grafana jaise dashboards) aur alerting (threshold cross ho to alert bhejo). User feedback bhi pipeline ka hissa hai — thumbs up/down, corrections — ye sabse valuable signal hai.

Kya log karein — checklist

  • Har request: prompt, response, model version, tokens, latency, cost.
  • RAG steps: retrieved chunks, scores, reranking.
  • Agent steps: plan, tool calls, observations, errors.
  • Errors: failures, timeouts, rate limits — stack trace ke saath.
  • User feedback: ratings, corrections, reports.
  • Mat bhoolo — PII mask karo: logs me personal data na aaye — ye privacy aur compliance ke liye zaroori hai.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 7: Evaluation for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous7.5 · Agentic systems ki evaluation — agents ko kaise test kareinNext →7.7 · Drift, feedback loops aur automated metrics
7.7Chapter 7 · Evaluation for LLMs

Drift, feedback loops aur automated metrics

Deploy karne ke baad kaam khatm nahi hota — duniya badalti hai, users badalte hain, data badalta hai. Drift wo phenomenon hai jab model ki performance dheere-dheere girti hai, bina kisi ko pata chale.

Drift ke types

  • Data drift: input data badal gaya — naye words, naye topics, naye user patterns. Model ne ye data training me nahi dekha tha.
  • Concept drift: "sahi" ka matlab hi badal gaya — jaise ek policy update hone se sahi jawaab badal jaye.
  • Model drift: provider ne model update kar diya — same prompt par alag output aane laga. Tumhare prompts aur evals us hisaab se toot sakte hain.

Drift kaise pakdein

  • Eval set ko continuously chalao: har din ya har hafte apna eval set production model par chalao — score girte hi alert aaye.
  • Input distribution monitor karo: naye topics ya languages aane par pata chale.
  • Output quality monitor karo: response length, refusal rate, user feedback — inme achanak badlav drift ka signal hai.
  • Embedding drift: input embeddings ka distribution badle to data drift hai.

Feedback loops — system ko khud seekhne do

User feedback (thumbs up/down, corrections, escalations) ko wapas system me dalo: eval set update karo, RAG documents update karo, prompts sudharo, fine-tuning data banao. Ye loop jitna tez hoga, system utni jaldi sudhrega. Lekin feedback ko blindly trust mat karo — noisy ya malicious feedback bhi aata hai, isliye human review ke saath use karo.

Automated metrics ki value

Human review achha hai lekin slow aur mehenga hai. Automated metrics (LLM judge, faithfulness scores, retrieval metrics) har request par chal sakte hain — real-time signals dete hain. Best practice: automated metrics se monitor karo, human review se validate karo — aur dono ke beech correlation dekhte raho. Agar automated metric aur human judgment alag hone lagein, to metric ko fix karo.

Evaluation frameworks

Evaluation ko ek framework me band karo — eval sets, metrics, dashboards aur alerts — taaki har change par evaluation automatic chale. Tools jaise LangSmith, Weights & Biases Weave aur open-source eval harnesses isme madad karte hain. Framework ka maksad hai: evaluation ek event nahi, ek habit bane.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 7: Evaluation for LLMs. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous7.6 · Logging aur observability — LLM system ke andar kya ho raha haiNext →8.1 · Governance kya hai — guardrails, compliance aur zimmedari
8.1Chapter 8 · Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, Security

Governance kya hai — guardrails, compliance aur zimmedari

Governance ka matlab hai: LLM application ko aise chalana ki wo safe, legal aur trustworthy rahe. Ye sirf security nahi hai — isme monitoring, privacy, compliance aur ethics — sab aate hain.

Governance ke 4 pillars

  • Monitoring: system kya kar raha hai, ye dekhna — performance, errors, misuse.
  • Privacy: user data ko protect karna — PII, consent, data residency.
  • Security: attacks se bachana — prompt injection, data leakage, unauthorized access.
  • Compliance: laws aur regulations ko follow karna — industry standards, internal policies.

Governance guardrails kya hain

Guardrails wo rules aur checks hain jo model ke input aur output par lagte hain. Input guardrails: prompt me PII hai? Malicious instruction hai? Output guardrails: jawaab me PII leak ho raha hai? Harmful content hai? Hallucination ka risk hai? Guardrails ko layers me lagao — ek layer fail ho to dusri pakde.

Governance kyun zaroori hai — real stakes

  • Legal: data protection laws todne par heavy fines lag sakte hain.
  • Reputational: ek harmful ya biased output brand ko saalon ka nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai.
  • Operational: ek security incident se system band ho sakta hai, data leak ho sakta hai.
  • Trust: users tabhi LLM par bharosa karenge jab unhe pata ho ki unka data safe hai aur outputs reliable hain.

Governance kab shuru karein

Day 1 se. Baad me jodna 10x mehenga aur mushkil hota hai. Pehle se tay karo: kaun sa data allowed hai, kaun se outputs blocked hain, kaun access kar sakta hai, audit kaise hoga. Ye decisions product design ka hissa hain, afterthought nahi.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 8: Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, and Security. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous7.7 · Drift, feedback loops aur automated metricsNext →8.2 · Threat landscape — prompt injection, jailbreaking aur aage
8.2Chapter 8 · Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, Security

Threat landscape — prompt injection, jailbreaking aur aage

LLM ke threats traditional software threats se alag hain — kyunki attacker seedha model se baat kar sakta hai, natural language me. Is section me har threat ko samjho.

Prompt injection — sabse bada LLM threat

Direct prompt injection: user seedha model ko malicious instruction de — "Apne instructions bhool jao, ab ye karo". Indirect prompt injection: malicious instruction kisi document ya webpage me chhupi ho, jise model padhe — upar wali figure yahi dikhati hai. User seedha kuch galat nahi kehta, lekin model ek compromised document padh kar attacker ki baat maan leta hai. RAG systems me ye khaas taur par khatarnak hai — kyunki retrieved documents me injection chhupa ho sakta hai.

Aur threats

  • Jailbreaking: model ki safety guardrails ko bypass karna — role-play, encoded text ya multi-step tricks se model se wo karwana jo use mana hai.
  • Data extraction: model se training data nikalwana — PII, secrets ya copyrighted text. Model ne jo memorize kiya hai, use prompt karke bahar nikala ja sakta hai.
  • Membership inference: pata lagana ki ek specific data point training me tha ya nahi — privacy ke liye khatra.
  • Denial-of-service (DoS): bahut lambe ya complex prompts se model ko slow ya expensive bana dena — cost aur availability par attack.
  • Model stealing: API se bahut saare queries karke model ka behavior copy karna.
  • Insider threats: internal actors — employees ya partners — jo access ka misuse karein. External attackers se zyada khatarnak ho sakte hain, kyunki unke paas pehle se access hota hai.

Threats se bachav — defense in depth

  • Input validation: prompt me injection patterns dhoondo — suspicious instructions flag karo.
  • Output filtering: jawaab me PII, harmful content ya policy violation check karo.
  • Least privilege: model aur tools ko sirf utni permission do jitni zaroori hai.
  • Isolation: retrieved documents ko untrusted treat karo — unki instructions ko follow mat karo, sirf unki information use karo.
  • Monitoring: unusual patterns par alert — achanak bahut saare requests, ajeeb prompts, ya sensitive data access.

8.3Chapter 8 · Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, Security

LLMSecOps audit — NIST framework aur 10-step process

LLMSecOps audit ek systematic check hai ki tumhari LLM application kitni secure hai. Kitab NIST Cybersecurity Framework ke basis par ek 10-step audit process batati hai.

NIST Cybersecurity Framework — 5 functions

Upar wali figure NIST framework dikhati hai — iske 5 core functions hain: Identify (kya protect karna hai), Protect (safeguards lagao), Detect (attacks pakdo), Respond (incident par action lo) aur Recover (normal par wapas aao). Ye framework har security program ki neev hai — LLM ke liye bhi wahi, LLM-specific threats ke saath.

10-step audit process

  1. Define scope and objectives: audit kis cheez ka hai — ek app, ek model, ya poora system? Objectives clear karo.
  2. Gather information: architecture, data flows, access patterns, policies — sab ikattha karo (aage section 8.4).
  3. Risk analysis and threat assessment: kaun se threats hain, kitna risk hai — prioritize karo.
  4. Evaluate security controls: jo controls lage hain, wo kaam kar rahe hain ya nahi?
  5. Perform penetration testing (red teaming): attacker ki tarah socho — model ko break karne ki koshish karo.
  6. Review model training and data: training data me PII, bias ya poisoned data to nahi?
  7. Assess model performance and bias: model biased ya unfair outputs to nahi de raha?
  8. Monitor and review: monitoring aur logging kaafi hai ya gaps hain?
  9. Document findings and recommendations: sab kuch likho — kya mila, kya fix karna hai.
  10. Communicate results and remediation plan: stakeholders ko batao, fix ka plan aur timeline tay karo.

Audit team — kaun hona chahiye

Audit team diverse honi chahiye: ML engineers aur security specialists (technical vulnerabilities), domain experts aur data scientists (data quality), product aur risk managers (strategic alignment), legal aur compliance officers (laws), external auditors aur end users (validation aur experience).

Audit ki cost aur timeline — kitab ke numbers

Audit typeTimelineCost (approx)
Simple app, single model2–4 weeks—
Enterprise-scale application1–3 months—
Regulatory deep audit3–6 months ya zyada$500,000+ tak
External audit (Phase I–II, steps 1–6)—$25,000–$250,000
Internal audit (Phase III, steps 7–10)—$5,000–$50,000 (staff time)

Ye numbers bade lagte hain, lekin audit na karne ki cost usse badi hoti hai — legal, financial, reputational damage aur regulatory fines. Aur kitab kehti hai: aaj ke time par poore 10-step process ke liye koi single end-to-end tool nahi hai — tumhe tools ko jodna padta hai.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 8: Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, and Security. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/

8.4Chapter 8 · Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, Security

Information gathering aur risk analysis

Audit ka step 2 aur 3 — information gathering aur risk analysis — poore audit ki neev hain. Bina sahi information ke, risk analysis galat hogi, aur bina risk analysis ke, audit bekaar hoga.

Information gathering — kya ikattha karein

  • Architecture diagrams: system kaise bana hai — components, data flows, integrations.
  • Data flows: data kahan se aata hai, kahan jata hai, kahan store hota hai — har hop par.
  • Access patterns: kaun kis cheez ko access kar sakta hai — users, services, tools.
  • Policies aur procedures: likhe hue rules — kya allowed hai, kya nahi.
  • Logs aur incidents: pehle kya hua — past incidents se bahut kuch seekhne ko milta hai.
  • Third-party dependencies: kaun se external services, models, libraries use ho rahe hain — unke risks bhi tumhare risks hain.

Risk analysis aur threat modeling — kaise karein

  1. Assets identify karo: kya protect karna hai — data, models, infrastructure, reputation.
  2. Threats list karo: section 8.2 ke threats me se kaun se tum par lagu hote hain?
  3. Vulnerabilities dhoondo: tumhare system me kamzoriyan kahan hain — code review, pen testing, red teaming se.
  4. Impact aur likelihood naapo: har threat ka impact kitna hoga (low/medium/high) aur hone ki probability kitni hai?
  5. Prioritize karo: high impact + high likelihood pehle — baaki baad me. Har risk ka owner tay karo.

Known risks vs unknown risks

Known risks wo hain jo tum jaante ho — jaise prompt injection. Unknown risks wo hain jo tum nahi jaante — naye attack techniques, naye model behaviors. Known risks ko controls se manage karo; unknown risks ke liye monitoring aur fast response capability rakho. Isi liye audit ek baar ka kaam nahi, regular process hai.

8.5Chapter 8 · Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, Security

Access control aur privacy — RBAC, PII aur data residency

Access control ka matlab hai: kaun kis cheez ko access kar sakta hai. Privacy ka matlab hai: user data ko kaise protect karte hain. Dono governance ke core hain.

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

Upar wali figure dikhati hai ki LLM application ke frontend me RBAC kaise kaam karta hai — har user ko ek role milti hai (admin, editor, viewer), aur har role ko specific permissions milti hain. Admin sab kuch kar sakta hai, viewer sirf dekh sakta hai. RBAC ke fayde: permissions manage karna aasan hai, least privilege enforce hota hai, aur audit me pata chalta hai ki kisne kya kiya.

Access control ke principles

  • Least privilege: har user/service ko sirf utni access do jitni uske kaam ke liye zaroori hai — zyada nahi.
  • Separation of duties: critical actions ke liye ek se zyada logon ki approval chahiye — jaise model deploy karne ke liye do approvals.
  • Regular review: permissions ko regularly review karo — jo access ab zaroori nahi, use hatao. Log jo company chhod gaye, unki access turant band karo.
  • Audit logs: har access ko log karo — kisne, kab, kya kiya. Audit ke waqt ye logs sabse valuable hote hain.

Privacy — PII aur data residency

  • PII handling: names, emails, phone numbers, addresses — inhe collect karne se pehle socho ki zaroorat hai ya nahi. Agar zaroorat hai to encrypt karo, access limit karo, aur retention policy rakho (kab delete karoge).
  • Consent: user data use karne se pehle consent lo — aur consent ko record rakho.
  • Data residency: data kahan store hota hai — kaun se country me? Kai regulations kehte hain ki citizen ka data usi country me rahe. Cloud region chunne se pehle ye check karo.
  • Geographic gaps: privacy laws har country me alag hain — jo ek jagah legal hai, wo dusri jagah illegal ho sakta hai. Global app banate waqt sabse strict law ko follow karo, ya region-wise policies rakho.
Training data aur privacy: model ko train karte waqt PII training data me na jaye — ye sabse mushkil privacy challenge hai, kyunki ek baar model ne PII memorize kar liya to use "delete" karna lagbhag impossible hai. Isliye PII ko training se pehle hi hatao.

8.6Chapter 8 · Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, Security

Monitoring aur incident response

Monitoring ka matlab hai system par nazar rakhna — aur incident response ka matlab hai jab kuch galat ho to kya karna hai. Dono ke bina governance adhuri hai.

Kya monitor karein — security lens se

  • Unusual prompts: injection patterns, jailbreak attempts, bahut lambe prompts — in par alert lagao.
  • Data access patterns: koi user achanak bahut saara sensitive data access kar raha hai? Ye exfiltration ka signal ho sakta hai.
  • Output anomalies: model achanak PII leak kar raha hai ya harmful content de raha hai?
  • Cost spikes: achanak cost badhna DoS ya misuse ka signal ho sakta hai.
  • Model behavior changes: provider ne model update kiya? Outputs badle?

Incident response plan — pehle se taiyaar rakho

  1. Detect: alert aaye to incident declare karo — severity tay karo (P1 critical, P2 high, P3 medium).
  2. Contain: damage ko roko — affected feature band karo, suspicious access revoke karo, model ko safe mode me dalo.
  3. Investigate: kya hua, kaise hua, kitna damage hua — logs aur traces se pata lagao.
  4. Remediate: fix karo — prompt guardrail lagao, data hatao, model update karo.
  5. Communicate: stakeholders aur (zaroorat ho to) users aur regulators ko batao — transparent raho.
  6. Learn: postmortem likho — kya seekha, aage kaise rokoge. Postmortem blameless hona chahiye.

Communication aur remediation plans

Audit ke step 10 me yehi aata hai — findings ko communicate karo aur remediation plan banao. Plan me hona chahiye: har finding, uski severity, fix ka owner, deadline, aur verification ka tareeka (fix hua ya nahi, ye kaise check karoge). Bina plan ke audit report sirf kagaz hai.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 8: Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, and Security. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/

8.7Chapter 8 · Governance: Monitoring, Privacy, Security

Guardrails aur responsible AI — HITL, bias aur documentation

Guardrails wo automated checks hain jo model ke output ko safe rakhte hain. Responsible AI isse bada concept hai — fairness, transparency aur accountability. Dono ke bina LLM application trustworthy nahi ban sakti.

Guardrails kaise lagayein — layers

  • Input layer: prompt me PII, injection ya harmful intent check karo — block karo ya flag karo.
  • Model layer: model ko safety training do (RLHF, constitutional approaches) — lekin is par bharosa mat karo, ye bypass ho sakta hai.
  • Output layer: jawaab ko filter karo — PII, toxic content, hallucination signals check karo.
  • Application layer: business rules lagao — jaise "medical advice hamesha disclaimer ke saath do".

Human-in-the-loop (HITL) reviews

High-stakes outputs par human review zaroori hai — model jawaab de, human approve kare, phir user ko jaye. HITL ke levels hain: full review (har output check ho), sampled review (kuch outputs randomly check hon), escalation only (sirf risky outputs human ko jayein). Risk ke hisaab se level chuno — medical ya financial advice me full review, internal summary me sampled review kaafi hai.

Bias assessment

  • Model performance aur bias assessment: audit ka step 7 — model alag groups ke liye alag behave to nahi kar raha? Eval set me diverse groups shamil karo.
  • Data bias: training data me bias hai to model me bhi aayega — data audit karo.
  • Feedback bias: human reviewers ke apne biases hote hain — reviewers diverse rakho, guidelines clear rakho.

Documentation — governance ki jaan

Har decision document karo: model kaun sa hai, data kahan se aaya, guardrails kya hain, audit kab hua, incidents kya hue. Documentation se hota hai: audit aasan hota hai, naye team members jaldi samajhte hain, aur jab kuch galat ho to pata chalta hai ki decision kisne, kyun liya tha. Model cards aur data sheets — ye documentation ke standard formats hain.

Ethics — challenge jo kabhi khatm nahi hota

LLM se jude ethical sawaal — bias, misinformation, job displacement, copyright — inka koi ek jawaab nahi hai. Lekin governance ka kaam hai in sawaalon ko discuss karna, policies banana aur unhe enforce karna. Responsible AI ek destination nahi, ek process hai.

9.1Chapter 9 · Scaling

Scaling ki challenge aur hardware — GPUs

Scaling ka matlab hai: LLM application ko zyada users, zyada data aur zyada load par chalana — bina performance ya cost ke bigde. Is chapter me scaling ka poora stack hai — hardware se lekar backup tak.

Scaling ki challenge — 3 dimensions

  • Compute scaling: zyada requests matlab zyada GPU compute — GPUs mehenga aur limited hain.
  • Memory scaling: bada model + lamba context = bahut memory — ek GPU me fit nahi hota.
  • Cost scaling: scale ke saath cost linearly badhti hai — bina optimization ke budget explode ho jata hai.

GPUs — khareedna ya kiraye par lena

OptionFaydeNuksaan
Buy (on-prem)Long-term me sasta (heavy use par), full control, data on-prem rehta haiBada upfront cost, maintenance tumhari, hardware purana padta hai
Rent (cloud)Zero upfront, flexible scale, latest hardware milta haiHeavy use par mehenga, vendor lock-in, data cloud me jata hai

Rule: usage unpredictable ho ya shuruaat ho to rent karo; usage stable aur heavy ho to buy karna socho. Kai teams hybrid karti hain — baseline load on-prem, spikes cloud par.

GPU provisioning aur management

  • Right-sizing: model ke hisaab se GPU chuno — chhote model ke liye bada GPU waste hai.
  • Utilization: GPU idle na rahe — batching aur multi-model serving se utilization badhao.
  • Monitoring: GPU memory, utilization, temperature — in par alerts lagao. Ek GPU fail ho to system ko pata chalna chahiye.
  • Kubernetes: owned hardware par bhi Kubernetes se GPU provisioning aur management automate hoti hai.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 9: Scaling: Hardware, Infrastructure, and Resource Management. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/

9.2Chapter 9 · Scaling

Compilers aur kernel fusion — hardware se zyada nikaalo

Compiler high-level code ko machine instructions me badalta hai — aur LLM workloads ke liye specialized compilers hardware se maximum performance nikalte hain. Ye scaling ka hidden lever hai.

Specialized compilers

  • NVCC (NVIDIA): CUDA code ke liye compiler — GPU programs ko optimize karta hai.
  • XLA (TensorFlow): TensorFlow graphs ko optimize karta hai — fusion aur memory planning ke saath.
  • TorchScript (PyTorch): PyTorch models ko optimized, deployable format me badalta hai.

3 types ki compiler optimizations

1. Kernel fusion

Multiple operations ko ek GPU kernel me combine kar do — taaki intermediate results ko global memory me likhna aur dobara padhna na pade. Example: ReLU(Wx + b) — matrix multiplication, bias add aur activation — teeno ko ek kernel me fuse kar do. Fayde: kam memory access (intermediate results fast registers/shared memory me rehte hain), kam kernel launch overhead, behtar cache efficiency.

2. Precision scaling

32-bit floating point (FP32) ki jagah 16-bit (FP16) ya brain float (BF16) use karo — memory aadhi, speed double (tensor cores par). Compilers mixed-precision training automate karte hain — critical operations (jaise gradient accumulation) FP32 me rehte hain, baaki FP16 me. Modern GPUs (A100, H100) me tensor cores lower precision ke liye optimize hain.

3. Hardware utilization

Compiler operations ko specialized units par map karta hai — tensor cores, matrix units, vector processors. Instruction-level parallelism se hazaron GPU threads aur vector operations ek saath chalte hain. Memory hierarchy (shared memory, registers, caches) ko efficiently use karna — global memory par kam depend karna — ye bhi compiler ka kaam hai.

Practical takeaway: tumhe compiler khud likhne ki zaroorat nahi hai — lekin ye samajhna zaroori hai ki tumhara framework (PyTorch, TensorFlow) in optimizations ko kaise use karta hai. Mixed precision on karo, fusion-friendly operations likho, aur latest framework versions use karo — inme compiler optimizations improve hoti rehti hain.
Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 9: Scaling: Hardware, Infrastructure, and Resource Management. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/

9.3Chapter 9 · Scaling

Parallel aur distributed computing — data, model, pipeline

Ek GPU par bada LLM train ya serve nahi hota — kaam ko kai GPUs ya nodes par baantna padta hai. Iske 3 main tareeke hain, aur inke building blocks hain CUDA aur NCCL.

Building blocks — CUDA aur NCCL

  • CUDA: NVIDIA ka GPU programming platform — matrix multiplication, attention, gradients — sab GPU par chalane ke liye APIs deta hai. Chhote models bhi acceptable performance ke liye CUDA par depend karte hain.
  • NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library): multiple GPUs ke beech communication optimize karta hai — all-reduce, all-gather, broadcast jaise operations minimal latency aur high bandwidth par. Distributed training me gradients ko GPUs ke beech sync karna NCCL ka kaam hai.

Data parallelism

Dataset ko chunks me baanto — har GPU ko ek chunk do, har GPU par model ki ek copy rakho. Har GPU apne chunk par gradients compute kare, phir gradients ko average karke (all-reduce) sab GPUs par model update karo. Simple aur effective — lekin model ek GPU ki memory me fit hona chahiye.

Model parallelism

Model ko hi baanto — har GPU ko model ka ek hissa (kuch layers) do. Input forward pass me GPUs se guzarta hai, backward pass me gradients reverse order me compute hote hain. Memory problem solve hoti hai, lekin throughput ghatti hai — ek GPU kaam kare to dusre wait karte hain.

Pipeline parallelism

Model ko layers ke hisaab se baanto (jaise model parallelism), lekin data batches ko micro-batches me todo — taaki saare devices ek saath busy rahein. Upar wali figure dikhati hai ki 4 devices par 4 micro-batches se pipeline kaise chalti hai. Implementation pehle mushkil tha, lekin 2022 me Meta ka PiPPy aaya, jo ab PyTorch me torch.distributed.pipelining ke roop me merged hai — alag install nahi chahiye.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 9: Scaling: Hardware, Infrastructure, and Resource Management. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous9.2 · Compilers aur kernel fusion — hardware se zyada nikaaloNext →9.4 · ZeRO aur DeepSpeed — memory optimization ke advanced frameworks
9.4Chapter 9 · Scaling

ZeRO aur DeepSpeed — memory optimization ke advanced frameworks

Model bada ho to memory hi sabse badi problem hoti hai. ZeRO aur DeepSpeed is problem ke sabse powerful solutions hain — inhe samajhna har LLMOps engineer ke liye zaroori hai.

ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer)

Microsoft ka ZeRO training ke dauraan memory overhead ko kam karta hai — model states (parameters, gradients, optimizer states) ko devices par partition karke. Har GPU sirf apna hissa store karta hai, duplicate nahi. Isse tens ya hundreds of billions of parameters wale models ko train kiya ja sakta hai bina bahut bade memory wale GPUs ke.

DeepSpeed

ZeRO par built, DeepSpeed ek deep-learning optimization library hai jo bade models ki training ko efficient banati hai: mixed-precision training, gradient accumulation, memory optimization — training time aur cost dono kam hote hain.

Memory optimization techniques — kitab ki Table 9-2

TechniqueKya problem solve karta haiKaise kaam karta haiTrade-off
ShardingModel ek GPU me fit nahi hotaWeights/layers kai GPUs par baantoSync aur communication complexity
Activation checkpointingBackprop me zyada memorySirf key activations save karo, baaki recompute karoExtra compute time
Dynamic batchingChhote requests par compute wasteInputs ko on-the-fly group karoHalki response delay
Model offloadingGPU poora model hold nahi kar saktaUnused parts CPU/disk par rakho, zaroorat par laoTransfer time se slow
Mixed precision trainingActivations aur weights zyada jagah lete hainFP16 use karo FP32 ki jagahHalki numerical accuracy loss (aksar negligible)
QuantizationModel deployment ke liye bahut bada haiWeights ko 8-bit ya kam me compress karoCareless use par accuracy loss
Gradient accumulationBatch size GPU me fit nahi hotiBade batch ko chhote chunks me baant kar gradients accumulate karoSlow iteration time
ZeROOptimizer state GPUs par duplicate hota haiOptimizer state aur gradients partition karoComplexity aur comm overhead
Operator fusionBahut saare chhote intermediate tensorsMultiple ops ek me combine karoCompiler/tooling support chahiye
Paged attention (inference)Lambe context me memory spikesKV cache ko virtual memory ki tarah stream karoSmart scheduling chahiye

Ye table poori kitab ki sabse useful tables me se ek hai — isse yaad rakho. Interview me poochha jata hai: "Model GPU me fit nahi ho raha, kya karoge?" — is table se jawaab do.

9.5Chapter 9 · Scaling

Testing strategies aur Infrastructure as Code

Scale par deploy karna risky hai — ek galat deploy hazaron users ko affect karta hai. Isliye testing strategies aur Infrastructure as Code (IaC) scaling ke must-have hain.

Testing strategies — deploy se pehle aur baad me

  • A/B testing: users ko do groups me baanto — ek ko purana model, dusre ko naya. Metrics compare karo — naya behtar hai to rollout badhao, nahi to wapas lo. LLM me A/B testing mushkil hai kyunki output non-deterministic hai — bade sample aur sahi metrics chahiye.
  • Shadow testing: naya model production traffic par chalao, lekin uska output user ko mat dikhao — sirf compare karo. Risk zero, learning poori.
  • Canary deployment: pehle 1% users par deploy karo, phir 5%, phir 25%, phir 100% — har stage par metrics dekho. Problem aaye to turant rollback karo.
  • Blue-green deployment: do environments rakho — blue (current) aur green (new). Green ko test karo, phir traffic switch karo. Rollback matlab traffic wapas blue par.

Infrastructure as Code (IaC)

IaC ka matlab hai: infrastructure ko code me likho — servers, networks, GPUs, configs — sab version-controlled files me. Fayde: reproducibility (same infra dobara banao), review (infra changes par bhi code review), rollback (purana version wapas lao), audit (kisne kya badla, pata chalta hai). Tools: Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation, Kubernetes manifests.

IaC aur LLMOps ka connection

LLM deployment me IaC aur bhi important hai — kyunki infra complex hai (GPUs, vector DBs, model files, caches). Bina IaC ke, "staging par chalta tha, production par kyun nahi" — ye problem roz aayegi. IaC files ko bhi backup karo — ye tumhare system ka blueprint hain (aage section 9.6).

Fault tolerance — system toote to kya ho

Ideal duniya me saare resources performance par lagte; real duniya me kuch resources fault tolerance par lagane padte hain — ye overhead cost hai. Retry logic, circuit breakers, fallbacks, health checks — ye sab fault tolerance ke tools hain. LLM systems me ek aur layer hai: model fail ho to chhota model ya cached response se kaam chalao (graceful degradation).

9.6Chapter 9 · Scaling

Backup aur failsafe — restore test karna backup se zyada important hai

LLM applications me LLMOps engineer backup ka zimmedar hota hai. Failures hote hain — hardware kharab, software bug, ya malicious activity. Backup aur failsafe strategies se continuity milti hai aur downtime kam hota hai.

Kya backup karein — stage ke hisaab se

  • Development me: training data, intermediate model weights (checkpoints), aur infrastructure-as-code files. Datasets aur checkpoints bahut bade hote hain, IaC files chhoti hoti hain.
  • Production me: production architecture ki IaC files, user data (query logs, personalizations) aur performance metrics. Preprocessed ya fine-tuning data khona bahut mehenga pad sakta hai — use bachana zaroori hai.

Backup ke 3 types

TypeKya karta haiRestore kaise hota hai
Full backupPoora dataset ya model ek point-in-time par capture karoSimple — ek backup se restore ho jata hai; lekin storage zyada lagta hai
Incremental backupSirf wo changes jo pichle backup (full ya incremental) ke baad huePoori sequence chahiye — ek bhi block missing ho to restore fail hoga; storage kam lagta hai
Differential backupWo changes jo pichle full backup ke baad hueLatest full + latest differential — dono chahiye; storage aur speed ka balance

Kaun sa backup chunna hai

  • High-stakes applications: frequent backups, redundancy, kam downtime — frequent full backups recommended hain.
  • Bada data volume: incremental ya differential se storage bachta hai — daily full copies mehenga hai (time aur storage dono me).
  • Compliance: kai industries me backup rakhna legal requirement hai — auditability aur accountability ke liye.
Sabse important baat: backup lena kaafi nahi hai — restore strategy ka hona aur use regularly test karna usse zyada important hai. Bahut se experienced practitioners ki "war stories" hain jahan saalon tak backups liye gaye, lekin jab zaroorat padi to restore kaam hi nahi kiya — kyunki kabhi test hi nahi hua tha. Apna restore har quarter test karo.

Storage tiers — hot, warm, cold

Backup storage ke 3 tiers hote hain: hot storage (turant access, mehenga — recent backups), warm storage (thodi der me access, medium cost), cold storage (ghanton me access, sasta — purane archives). Sahi tier chunne se cost bahut bachti hai.

10.1Chapter 10 · The Future of LLMs and LLMOps

Scaling ka future — compute-optimal aur aage

Chapter 10 kitab ka aakhri chapter hai — future ki taraf dekhta hai. Pehla sawaal: scaling aage kaise badhega?

Scaling law — dobara, future ke context me

Upar wali figure scaling law dikhati hai — N (data points ki sankhya) aur D (dataset size) ke saath performance kaise badhti hai. Future me scaling sirf "bada model" nahi hoga — compute-optimal training hoga: fixed budget me model size aur data ka best balance. Chinchilla approach (Chapter 5.8) isi ka example hai — chhota model + zyada data, bade model + kam data se behtar.

Scaling ke 3 future directions

  • Efficient scaling: MoE, sparse models, distillation — kam compute me zyada capability. Model bada hoga, lekin har query par sirf ek hissa chalega.
  • Data scaling: data quality aur diversity par focus — synthetic data, curated data, multimodal data. Data hi naya bottleneck hai — achha data khatm ho raha hai.
  • Inference scaling: training se zyada, inference time par compute badhana — chain-of-thought, self-consistency, multi-sample voting. Model ko "sochne" ka zyada time do, behtar jawaab milega.

Scaling ki limits

Scaling hamesha kaam nahi karega — data khatm ho sakta hai, energy cost badh sakti hai, aur kuch capabilities scale se nahi aati (jaise true reasoning ya common sense). Isliye future me scaling ke saath architecture innovation bhi chahiye — naye designs, naye training methods.

10.2Chapter 10 · The Future of LLMs and LLMOps

Reliability ka future — hallucination se trust tak

Reliability LLMOps ka key goal hai — aur future me ye aur bhi important hoga, kyunki LLMs critical decisions me use honge.

Reliability ki challenge — ek example se

Upar wali figure ek bade tech company ke LLM ka example dikhati hai — itni badi company, itna bada model, phir bhi reliability ki struggle hai. Isse pata chalta hai ki reliability scale ya budget se nahi aati — ye ek systematic problem hai jo har team ko solve karni hai, chhoti ho ya badi.

Reliability badhane ke future tareeke

  • Grounding: model ke jawaab ko trusted sources se jodo — RAG, citations, verifiable outputs. Jawaab ke saath "ye kahan se aaya" bhi do.
  • Self-verification: model apne jawaab ko khud check kare — dusra pass, dusra model, ya tools se verify karo.
  • Uncertainty: model ko apni uncertainty batani chahiye — "mujhe iska jawaab nahi pata" kehna, galat jawaab dene se behtar hai. Abstention ek feature hai, bug nahi.
  • Human oversight: high-stakes decisions me human review hamesha rahega — model assist karega, decide nahi karega.

Trust kaise banta hai

Trust ek din me nahi banta — consistent performance, transparent limitations, aur honest errors se banta hai. Apne users ko batao ki model kya kar sakta hai aur kya nahi — overpromise mat karo. Aur jab model galat ho, use chhupao mat — acknowledge karo aur fix karo.

10.3Chapter 10 · The Future of LLMs and LLMOps

Hybrid architectures — neurosymbolic, memory-augmented, MoE

Future ke LLMs sirf Transformer nahi honge — hybrid architectures aayenge jo neural networks ko dusri techniques se jodenge. Kitab 7 hybrid directions batati hai.

7 hybrid directions

  • Neurosymbolic (hybrid) architectures: neural networks + symbolic reasoning (rules, logic) — model facts yaad rakhe aur logic se reason kare. Maths aur structured reasoning me behtar hoga.
  • Memory-augmented models: model ke paas external memory ho — jaise ek notebook jisme wo facts likh kar rakh sake aur baad me use kar sake. Lambi conversations aur complex tasks me ye game-changer hoga.
  • MoE models: Mixture of Experts (Chapter 5.8) — scale ka future. Har query par sirf relevant experts chalein.
  • Multimodal fine-tuning: text, image, audio — sab par ek saath fine-tune karo — model har modality ko samajhe.
  • Cross-model collaboration: kai models ek saath kaam karein — ek plan kare, dusra execute kare, teesra verify kare.
  • Meta-learning: model seekhna seekhe — naye task par kam examples me adapt ho jaye.
  • Self-optimizing models: model khud apne prompts, apne tools aur apne behavior ko improve kare — human intervention kam ho.
  • Sparse models: model ke zyadatar parameters har query par inactive rahein — efficiency badhe, cost ghate.

Hybrid ka matlab LLMOps ke liye

Har hybrid component ek naya Ops surface hai — memory ko manage karna, experts ko balance karna, multi-model collaboration ko monitor karna. LLMOps engineer ka kaam aur complex hoga, lekin tools bhi behtar honge. Jo aaj RAG aur agents ke liye seekh rahe ho, wahi skills hybrid future me kaam aayengi.

10.4Chapter 10 · The Future of LLMs and LLMOps

GPU, data aur privacy ka future

Hardware, data aur privacy — teeno ka future LLMs ke future ko shape karega. Is section me teeno par ek nazar hai.

GPU performance ka future

Upar wali figure agle 30 saal me GPU performance ka prediction dikhati hai — trend upar ki taraf hai, lekin growth rate aur naye bottlenecks (energy, memory bandwidth, chip size) bhi dikhte hain. GPU advances se models bade aur tez honge, lekin LLMOps ki zaroorat khatm nahi hogi — hardware behtar hoga, lekin systems complex bhi honge.

Data management ka future

  • Synthetic data: model se data generate karwao — real data ki kami ko poora karo. Lekin synthetic data ke apne risks hain — model apni galtiyan khud reinforce kar sakta hai.
  • Data-centric AI: focus model se hat kar data par aayega — data quality, data versioning, data governance — ye LLMOps ka core banega.
  • Federated learning: data ko move kiye bina, distributed training — privacy ke liye behtar, lekin complex.

Privacy aur security ka future

  • On-device LLMs: chhote models phone aur laptop par chalenge — data device se bahar hi nahi jayega. Privacy ka sabse behtar solution.
  • Confidential computing: encrypted data par compute karo — cloud provider bhi data nahi dekh sakta.
  • Regulations badhenge: AI laws aayenge aur strict honge — governance aur audit (Chapter 8) aur bhi important ho jayenge.
  • Watermarking aur provenance: AI-generated content ko mark karo — taaki pata chale ki ye AI ne banaya hai.

10.5Chapter 10 · The Future of LLMs and LLMOps

Evaluation frameworks ka future

Evaluation ka future automated, continuous aur comprehensive hoga — aur LLMOps ka ek core hissa ban jayega.

Evaluation me kya badlega

  • Comprehensive frameworks: aaj ke tools alag-alag metrics dete hain; future me ek framework sab kuch dega — quality, safety, bias, cost, latency — ek dashboard par.
  • Continuous evaluation: har deploy, har prompt change, har data update par evaluation automatic chalegi — CI/CD ka hissa ban jayegi.
  • Real-world evals: benchmarks se hat kar, real user tasks par evaluation — jo actually matter karta hai.
  • Agent evals mature honge: aaj agent evaluation mushkil hai; future me standard rubrics aur harnesses aayenge.
  • Human + AI judges: human review aur LLM judges ka combination — human ground truth dega, AI scale dega.

LLMOps ka future — kitab ka conclusion

Kitab ka aakhri message ye hai: LLMOps ka future LLMs ke future ke saath juda hai. Jaise-jaise models capable honge, waise-waise unhe chalana aur complex hoga — aur LLMOps engineers ki demand badhegi. Jo skills is kitab me hain — data, deployment, evaluation, governance, scaling — ye aane wale saalon me aur bhi valuable honge.

Kitab ka core message: LLM ko demo me chalana aasan hai; production me reliably, securely aur affordably chalana hi asli skill hai — aur wahi LLMOps hai.
