10.6Chapter 10 · The Future of LLMs and LLMOps

LLMOps engineer ke roop me succeed kaise karein

Kitab ka aakhri section career par hai — LLMOps engineer ke roop me succeed karne ke liye kya chahiye. Ye sirf technical skills nahi, ek mindset hai.

Technical skills — hamesha update rakho

  • Core: Python, APIs, Docker, Kubernetes, cloud, CI/CD, monitoring — ye foundation hai, kabhi purana nahi hoga.
  • LLM-specific: prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, evaluation, vector DBs — ye har saal badlega, isliye seekhte raho.
  • Systems thinking: poora system dekho — model, data, infra, security — ek saath. Ek component ko optimize karna kaafi nahi, system ko optimize karna hai.

Non-technical skills — jo aksar miss hote hain

  • Communication: technical cheezein non-technical stakeholders ko samjhana — cost, risk, trade-offs ko simple bhasha me batana.
  • Documentation: jo likha hai, wahi bachta hai — decisions, incidents, runbooks — sab document karo.
  • Incident handling: pressure me calm rehna, systematic debug karna, blameless postmortem likhna.
  • Business sense: har technical decision ka business impact samajhna — cost, revenue, risk.

Career path — kahan se kahan tak

  • Shuruaat: MLOps ya software engineering se — LLMOps skills jodo, ek RAG app deploy karo.
  • Mid-level: production LLM systems own karo — evaluation, governance, scaling — sab sambhalo.
  • Senior: architecture decisions, team mentoring, org-level LLMOps strategy.
  • Aage: AI platform, AI infrastructure, ya AI safety — specialization ke kai raste hain.

Aakhri advice — kitab se

Field bahut tez badal raha hai — jo aaj cutting-edge hai, wo kal basic hoga. Isliye seekhna kabhi band mat karo: papers padho, experiments karo, community me raho, aur apne projects ko production me le jao. Aur yaad rakho — LLMOps ka maksad technology nahi, trust hai: users ka trust ki system sahi, safe aur reliable hai.

Is SPA me tumne poori kitab padh li — 10 chapters, 70 sections, 29 figures, 8 labs, 36 FAQs. Ab labs karo, FAQs revise karo, aur apna pehla LLMOps project shuru karo.

Source:Source: LLMOps (O'Reilly Media, Inc., 2025) — Chapter 10: The Future of LLMs and LLMOps. https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/llmops/9781098154202/
← Previous10.5 · Evaluation frameworks ka future
L1Interactive Lab

Tokenizer Lab — Text kitne tokens me tootta hai?

Neeche koi bhi text likho — lab use tokens me todega, token count batayega aur cost ka estimate dega. Yehi wajah hai ki LLM ka context window aur billing tokens me naapa jata hai, words me nahi.

LAB 1Tokenizer — subword tokenization
Tokens

Rule of thumb: English me 1 token ≈ 4 characters ≈ 0.75 word. 100 tokens ≈ 75 words. Rare/lambe words kai tokens me toot te hain — isliye unki cost zyada padti hai.

L2Interactive Lab

Prompt Lab — Temperature aur prompt style ka asar

Ek hi sawaal ko alag temperature par poochho aur dekho ki output kaise badalta hai. Temperature 0 ke paas matlab deterministic (hamesha same jawaab), zyada temperature matlab creative aur varied — lekin galti ka risk bhi zyada.

LAB 2Prompting — temperature explorer
Model ka jawab (simulated — kitab ke concepts par based)

Rule: factual kaam (hisab, extraction) me temperature 0–0.3 rakho; brainstorming ya writing me 0.7–1.0; 1.5+ par output unpredictable ho jata hai — production me kabhi mat rakho.

L3Interactive Lab

RAG Lab — Retrieve, rerank, generate — step by step

Ek chhota knowledge base diya gaya hai. Apna sawaal likho — lab dikhayega ki kaun se documents retrieve hue (score ke saath), reranking ne order kaise badla, aur final jawaab kaise bana. Retrieval kharab ho to jawaab bhi kharab — yehi RAG ki jaan hai.

LAB 3RAG pipeline — live stepper
Step 1 — Retrieval (top-3, similarity score)
Step 2 — Rerank ke baad
Step 3 — Generated jawaab (sirf retrieved context se)

Scoring yahan keyword overlap se hoti hai (asli systems me embeddings use hote hain). Reranker exact phrase match ko boost karta hai — dekho order kaise badalta hai.

L4Interactive Lab

Cost Lab — Fine-tuning vs prompting: kab kya sasta hai?

Kitab ki analogy yaad karo: fine-tuning upfront payment hai, prompt engineering mortgage hai. Is calculator me apne numbers dalo — dekho kitne mahine me fine-tuning sasti padti hai, aur kab prompting hi behtar rehti hai.

LAB 4Cost calculator — fine-tune vs prompt
Result

Rates illustrative hain — kitab ka real number: GPT-4o fine-tuning $25,000 per million tokens (kitab ke likhte waqt). Apne provider ke actual rates se replace karo. Model lifespan sabse important input hai: lifespan chhota ho to fine-tuning kabhi payback nahi karti.

L5Interactive Lab

Metrics Lab — Precision, recall, F1, hit rate, MRR nikalo

Evaluation metrics ko haath se nikalo — classification ke liye TP/FP/FN dalo, retrieval ke liye ranked list dalo (1 = relevant, 0 = irrelevant). Dekho ki accuracy kab dhokha deti hai aur F1 kab imaandar hota hai.

LAB 5Evaluation metrics — calculator
Result

Accuracy dhokha deti hai: 1000 me se 890 TN hon to "sab negative bolo" wala model bhi 89% accurate hoga — lekin ek bhi positive nahi pakdega. Isliye precision, recall aur F1 dekho.

L6Interactive Lab

SLO Lab — Uptime, error budget aur latency SLO

Apna SLO dalo aur dekho ki kitna downtime allowed hai, error budget kitna bachta hai, aur latency percentiles SLO pass karte hain ya nahi. Yehi numbers production decisions chalate hain.

LAB 6SLO / error budget — calculator
Result

99.9% SLO ka matlab hai mahine me sirf ~43 minutes downtime allowed hai. 99.99% par sirf ~4.3 minutes. Har extra 9 cost ko 10x badha deta hai — isliye SLO business need ke hisaab se tay karo, "zyada 9 behtar" ke hisaab se nahi.

L7Interactive Lab

MoE Lab — Tokens experts me kaise route hote hain?

Mixture of Experts me gating network har token ko 1-2 experts ke paas bhejta hai. Is simulator me tokens bhejo aur dekho: bina load balancing ke kuch experts overload hote hain aur baaki idle rehte hain — load-balancing loss se distribution kaise sudharta hai.

LAB 7MoE router — load balancing simulator
Har expert ko mile tokens

Asli MoE me gating network token ke hidden state se har expert ko ek score deta hai. GShard top-2 experts chunta hai, Switch Transformer top-1. Load balancing ke bina expert collapse hota hai — kuch experts sab kaam karte hain, baaki waste hote hain.

L8Interactive Lab

Deployment Lab — Kitne GPUs aur replicas chahiye?

Apne traffic ke numbers dalo — QPS, tokens per request, aur ek GPU ki throughput — lab batayega ki kitne replicas chahiye, kitne GPUs lagenge, aur monthly cost kitni aayegi. Yehi sizing production planning ki shuruaat hai.

LAB 8Deployment sizing — calculator
Result

Throughput aur price illustrative example values hain — apne model aur cloud provider ke actual numbers dalo. Headroom spikes ke liye rakho: bina headroom ke ek traffic spike par p95 latency explode ho jati hai.

FInterview FAQs

Interview FAQs — 36 sawaal

LLMOps interviews me sabse zyada poochhe jaane wale sawaal — kitab ke har chapter se, Hinglish me jawab ke saath.

Q1LLM kya hota hai aur ye traditional ML models se kaise alag hai?
LLM ek bada neural network hai jo massive text data par train hota hai aur bhasha samajh kar naya text generate kar sakta hai. Traditional ML models zyadatar discriminative hote hain — wo classify ya predict karte hain (spam hai ya nahi). LLM generative hain — wo content banate hain. Dusra farq scale hai: LLM me billions of parameters hote hain, jabki traditional models me thousands ya millions. Teesra farq: LLM ek hi model se kai tasks kar sakta hai (likhna, summarize, code, Q&A) bina har task ke liye alag training ke — ye general-purpose nature hi inhe revolutionary banati hai.
Q2Transformer architecture me self-attention ka matlab kya hai?
Self-attention ek mechanism hai jisme model sentence ke har word ko samajhne ke liye baaki words ko dekhta hai aur har word ko ek importance score deta hai. Example: 'Bank ke paas nadi hai' me 'bank' ka matlab samajhne ke liye model 'nadi' par zyada attention dega. Ye attention weights training me seekhe jate hain. Multi-head attention me kai heads ek saath alag-alag relations pakadte hain. Self-attention ki cost sequence length ke square se badhti hai, isliye lamba context mehenga padta hai — yehi wajah hai ki KV-caching aur efficient attention jaise optimizations important hain.
Q3Open-weight LLM aur proprietary LLM me se kaun sa chunna chahiye?
Ye tumhare use case par depend karta hai. Proprietary API models (jaise GPT-4, Claude) sabse capable hain, turant shuru ho jate hain aur infrastructure nahi chahiye — lekin per-token cost hoti hai, data provider ke paas jata hai aur model kabhi bhi badal sakta hai. Open-weight models (jaise LLaMA family) me data tumhare paas rehta hai, full control aur custom fine-tuning milti hai — lekin GPU infra aur maintenance tumhari zimmedari hai. Rule: pehle API se validate karo, phir decide karo ki self-host karna worth hai ya nahi. Sensitive data ya heavy usage ho to open model, speed aur capability chahiye to API.
Q4LLMOps kya hai aur ye MLOps se kaise alag hai?
LLMOps wo practices aur tools hain jo LLM applications ko production me develop, deploy, monitor aur maintain karne ke liye use hote hain. MLOps se 8 key differences hain: model size (billions of parameters), unstructured text data, non-deterministic output (same prompt, alag output), mushkil evaluation (sahi jawaab ek nahi), naye artifacts (prompts, embeddings, vector DB), poori pipeline deployment (model + retrieval + tools), aur naye security risks (prompt injection, jailbreaking, hallucination). MLOps ki neev — CI/CD, versioning, monitoring — same rehti hai, lekin LLM-specific layers upar jud jati hain.
Q5LLMOps ke 4 goals kaun se hain aur ye kyun important hain?
4 goals hain: Security (regulatory, reputational aur operational risks minimize karna), Scalability (demand par efficiently scale karna, latency/throughput/cost optimize karke), Robustness (galat ya adversarial input par bhi sahi behave karna) aur Reliability (predictable, consistent behavior — hallucination aur bias se bachna). Ye goals har LLMOps decision ko drive karte hain — model chunna ho, deployment design ho ya monitoring setup. Ye goals kabhi-kabhi takrate bhi hain (zyada security se latency badh sakti hai), to engineer ka kaam hai business context ke hisaab se balance karna.
Q6MLOps engineer LLMOps me kaise shift kar sakta hai?
Tumhare MLOps skills — Python, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, monitoring, cloud — sab kaam aayenge. Naya seekhna hoga: LLM basics (Transformer, tokens, embeddings), prompt engineering, RAG aur vector databases, LLM evaluation metrics, aur LLM-specific security (prompt injection, guardrails). Kitab ka suggested order hai: pehle LLM basics, phir RAG + prompting ek real project ke saath, phir evaluation, phir security. Ek deployed RAG app ya fine-tuned model ka demo, certificates se zyada weight rakhta hai — interview me projects dikhao.
Q7SLO, SLA aur KPI me kya farq hai? Error budget kya hota hai?
SLO internal target hai (jaise 99.9% requests 2 second me respond karein). SLA customer ko diya gaya contractual promise hai — todne par penalty hoti hai, isliye SLA hamesha SLO se thoda loose rakha jata hai. KPI business metric hai (jaise cost per request, task success rate). Error budget SLO aur 100% ke beech ka gap hai — 99.9% SLO ka matlab 0.1% requests fail ho sakti hain. Ye budget batata hai ki tum kitna risk le sakte ho: budget bacha ho to naye features deploy karo, khatm ho gaya ho to stability par focus karo.
Q8LLMOps maturity model ke levels kaun se hain?
3 levels hain. Level 0 — No LLMOps: koi formal structure ya process nahi, sab ad-hoc hai. Level 1 — MLOps, no LLMOps: MLOps practices apply hote hain lekin LLM-specific adaptations nahi — prompts, RAG, hallucination monitoring cover nahi hote. Level 2 — Full LLMOps: mature state — advanced documentation, robust monitoring aur compliance, sophisticated orchestration aur human review, comprehensive risk evaluation (bias, fairness, drift) mitigation strategies ke saath. Zyadatar organizations aaj Level 0 ya 1 par hain. Level up karne ke liye ek saath sab mat karo — har quarter ek dimension ko Level 2 tak le jao.
Q9MCP (Model Context Protocol) kya hai aur ye kyun zaroori hai?
MCP ek open protocol hai jo LLM applications ko external tools aur data sources se standard tareeke se jodta hai. Isse pehle har tool ka alag integration likhna padta tha; MCP ne use standard bana diya — jaise USB port. Iske 3 main components hain: Host (LLM chalane wali app), Client (Host ke andar, ek server se baat karta hai) aur Server (tools, resources, prompts expose karta hai). Kaam 3 phases me hota hai: handshake (capabilities exchange), discovery (kaun se tools available hain) aur interaction (tool call aur result). Security me dhyan do: tools ko least-privilege par chalao, kyunki compromised tool poori system ko nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai.
Q10A2A protocol kya hai aur MCP se kaise alag hai?
A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol agents ke beech standard communication ke liye hai — jab ek agent dusre agent ko task de ya usse result le. MCP LLM ko tools/data se jodta hai (LLM ↔ Tool), A2A agent ko agent se jodta hai (Agent ↔ Agent). Ye competitors nahi, complements hain: ek multi-agent system me har agent apne tools se MCP ke through judta hai, aur agents aapas me A2A ke through baat karte hain. A2A me agent discovery (agent card), task bhejna, progress updates aur result wapas aana — ye steps hote hain. Challenges: trust (dusre agent ke output ko verify karo), error propagation aur cost.
Q11Agentic systems ki sabse badi mushkilein kaun si hain?
Kitab 5 mushkilein batati hai. Pehli: planning weak hai — agents multi-step tasks me bhatak jate hain. Dusri: reproducibility nahi hai — 10-step task dobara chalao to alag step par fail ho sakta hai, koi clear stack trace nahi hota. Teesri: memory bottleneck — facts store aur retrieve karna latency aur accuracy dono me mushkil hai, aur memory systems brittle aur leaky hote hain. Chauthi: lambi tasks me context bhool jana. Paanchvi: cost — har step ek LLM call hai. Practical advice: agents ko narrow, well-defined tasks do aur har agent ke liye human escalation path rakho.
Q12Multimodal LLM kya hota hai aur iski challenges kya hain?
Multimodal LLM text ke saath image, audio aur video bhi samajh sakta hai. Har modality ka apna encoder hota hai jo use vectors me badalta hai, phir ye vectors ek shared space me aate hain jahan LLM unhe ek saath samajhta hai. Use cases: image description, document scanning, visual Q&A, voice assistants, video summary, cross-modal search. Challenges: embeddings ko align karna mushkil hai, data aur compute cost zyada hai, evaluation ke liye text metrics kaafi nahi hain, aur security me naye attacks hain — jaise image me chhupa prompt injection. Agar text se kaam chal jaye to text se shuru karo.
Q13Data engineering LLM ke liye kyun itni important hai?
Kyunki LLM ki quality uske data ki quality se tay hoti hai — kachra data andar, kachra behavior bahar. Data engineering raw data ko model ke khane layak banati hai: collect, clean, dedup, decontaminate, PII remove, tokenize, embed aur index karna. LLM data traditional ML data se alag hai — unstructured text, massive volume (trillions of tokens), aur quality issues (duplicates, toxic content, bias, outdated info). Data par kharch kiya gaya ek ghanta, model debugging ke 10 ghante bachata hai. RAG ho ya fine-tuning — dono ki neev data engineering hi hai.
Q14DELC (Data Engineering Lifecycle) ke 5 stages kaun se hain?
5 stages hain: (1) Generation — data paida hota hai (users, sensors, transactions); (2) Storage — data kahan rakha jayega (lake, warehouse, vector DB); (3) Ingestion — data ko source se storage tak lana (batch ya streaming); (4) Transformation — raw ko usable banana (cleaning, dedup, enrichment, embedding); (5) Serving — data ko consumers tak pahunchana (training, RAG retrieval, dashboards). Inke aas-paas undercurrents hain: security, data management, DataOps, architecture, orchestration aur software engineering — ye har stage par lagte hain.
Q15Vector database kya hai aur RAG me iski kya role hai?
Vector database embeddings (vectors) ko store karke meaning-based search deti hai. Normal database keyword se dhoondti hai, vector database meaning se — 'billi' likho to cat, kitten, pet wale documents bhi milenge. RAG me flow hai: user ke sawaal ka embedding banao, vector DB se sabse similar chunks dhoondo, unhe context me model ko do. Chunne ke criteria: scale (kitne vectors), latency, metadata filtering, managed vs self-hosted, aur cost. Graph databases isse ek step aage hain — wo entities aur relationships store karte hain, jisse Graph RAG complex sawaalon me behtar hota hai.
Q16Deduplication aur decontamination me kya farq hai?
Deduplication ka matlab hai duplicate data hatana — exact dedup (bilkul same text) aur near dedup (lagbhag same text). Duplicate data se model us text ko zyada weight de deta hai aur memorization badhti hai. Decontamination ka matlab hai test data ko training data se alag rakhna — agar model ne test ke sawaal pehle dekh liye, to uska test score jhootha hoga. Dono quality ke liye zaroori hain: dedup model ko balanced rakhta hai, decontamination evaluation ko imaandar rakhta hai. N-gram overlap check se contamination pakda jata hai.
Q17Fine-tuning ke liye instruction dataset kaise banayein?
Instruction datasets 'instruction → response' pairs hote hain. Banane ke 4 tareeke: (1) Human-written — experts likhte hain, sabse high quality lekin mehenga; (2) Existing data se convert — FAQs, tickets, docs ko instruction format me badlo; (3) Automatically generate — bade LLM se generate karwao, phir quality check karo; (4) User interactions se — real conversations (consent aur privacy ke saath). Golden rules: quality > quantity (1,000 achhe examples 100,000 bekaar se behtar), diversity rakho, format consistent rakho, eval set alag rakho, aur iterate karo — pehle chhota dataset, evaluate karo, phir badhao.
Q18Training from scratch kab karna chahiye aur kab nahi?
Training from scratch sirf tab karo jab: (1) tumhari bhasha ya domain ke liye koi pretrained model hi nahi hai, (2) data, architecture aur training par full control chahiye (research/strategic reason), ya (3) existing models ki license tumhare use case ko allow nahi karti. Baaki sab cases me pretrained model lo aur adapt karo — fine-tuning, RAG ya prompting se. Scratch se training months aur millions kharch karti hai, aur usme stability, debugging aur cost ki badi challenges hain. Practical rule: pehle pretrained + LoRA try karo, wahi 95% cases me kaafi hota hai.
Q19LoRA kya hai aur ye full fine-tuning se kaise alag hai?
LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) ek PEFT technique hai: model ke weights freeze karke, unke saath chhote adapter matrices jodta hai — sirf adapters train hote hain. Ek 7B model ko fine-tune karne ke liye sirf kuch million parameters train karne padte hain — GPU memory aur time dono bahut kam. Full fine-tuning me saare billions parameters update hote hain — powerful lekin mehenga, aur catastrophic forgetting ka risk zyada. LoRA me base model freeze rehta hai to forgetting kam hoti hai, aur ek base + kai adapters se multi-task aasan hota hai. Rule: pehle LoRA try karo, full fine-tuning tab jab LoRA se kaam na chale.
Q20Fine-tuning aur prompt engineering me se kab kya chunna hai?
Prompt engineering model ko context deti hai (wo kya jaanta hai), fine-tuning uska behavior badalti hai (wo kaise kaam karta hai). Cost me: fine-tuning upfront mehenga hai, prompt engineering har request par mehenga hai (lamba prompt = zyada tokens) — kitab ki analogy: fine-tuning upfront payment hai, prompt engineering mortgage hai. Model ki lifespan bhi dekho: agar model 2 saal me badal jayega to 10 saal ke liye prepay karna bewakoofi hai. Example: specific XML format me output chahiye to fine-tuning behtar hai. Rule: dono available hon to pehle prompt engineering try karo — kuch ghanton me pata chal jayega; fine-tuning tab jab prompt se kaam na chale.
Q21Mixture of Experts (MoE) kya hai aur ye kaise kaam karta hai?
MoE me ek bade model ke andar kai chhote expert sub-networks hote hain. Har input ke liye ek gating network tay karta hai ki kaun se experts kaam karein — baaki soye rehte hain. Isse model trillions of parameters ka ho sakta hai lekin har query par sirf ek chhota hissa chalta hai — compute cost low rehti hai. GShard top-2 experts choose karta hai (zyada expressive, zyada communication), Switch Transformer top-1 (hard routing, kam communication). Sabse badi challenge load balancing hai — gating sab kaam kuch experts ko de de to baaki waste hote hain, isliye training me load-balancing loss add kiya jata hai.
Q22API-first deployment kya hai aur iske fayde kya hain?
API-first ka matlab hai LLM application ko pehle ek API ke roop me design karo — contract tay karo, phir implementation banao. Fayde: decoupling (model badlo, frontend ko pata nahi chalega), reusability (ek API ko web, mobile, internal tools — sab use kar sakte hain), scalability (API ko independently scale karo) aur testing (API contract par test likhna aasan hai). LLM APIs 3 types ki hoti hain: model APIs (seedha model call), platform APIs (tools + monitoring ke saath) aur LLMs-as-APIs (khud ka model host karke API banao). API design me versioning, rate limiting, auth aur streaming — chaaron zaroori hain.
Q23LLM API me rate limiting aur versioning kyun zaroori hai?
Rate limiting batata hai ki ek user kitne requests kar sakta hai — jaise 100 per minute. Isse DoS attacks rukte hain, ek user dusre ka resource nahi khata aur cost control me rehti hai. Limit cross ho to 429 error do. Versioning isliye zaroori hai kyunki API badlegi — naya model, naya format. Version rakho (v1, v2) taaki purane clients na tootein: naya version aaye, purana deprecated ho, phir notice dekar sunset ho. Model version aur API version dono track karo, kyunki model update se behavior badal sakta hai.
Q24LLM inference ki latency kaise kam karein?
5 tareeke hain. (1) KV caching — attention ke key-value tensors save karke reuse karo, generation 2-5x tez hoti hai. (2) Dynamic batching — kai requests ko ek batch me process karo, GPU utilization badhta hai. (3) Quantization — weights ko 16-bit ya 8-bit me chalao, memory kam aur speed zyada. (4) Serving frameworks — Triton, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM — ye paged attention aur continuous batching se throughput badhate hain. (5) Speculative decoding — chhota model draft kare, bada model verify kare. Measure karte waqt TTFT (time to first token), inter-token latency aur p95/p99 dekho — average nahi.
Q25LLM evaluation traditional ML evaluation se kyun mushkil hai?
5 reasons hain. Pehla: ek sawaal ke kai sahi jawaab hote hain — 'Paris kya hai?' ka jawaab do tareeke se sahi ho sakta hai. Dusra: output non-deterministic hai — same prompt par alag output aa sakta hai. Teesra: quality subjective hai — fluency, coherence, factuality alag dimensions hain. Chautha: hallucination — model confident hokar galat bol sakta hai, aur fluent galat jawaab pakadna mushkil hai. Paanchva: cost — achhi evaluation me human review ya bade LLM judges chahiye. Isliye evaluation 3 layers me hoti hai: offline (deploy se pehle), online (production me) aur continuous (har change par).
Q26BLEU, ROUGE aur BERTScore me kya farq hai aur kab kaun sa use karein?
BLEU aur ROUGE n-gram based metrics hain — generated text aur expected answer ke beech word sequences ka overlap dekhte hain. BLEU machine translation ke liye, ROUGE summarization ke liye use hota hai. Inki problem: 'The capital of France is Paris' sahi hone par bhi expected answer 'Paris' se sirf 16.6% match karega. BERTScore similarity based hai — embeddings se meaning compare karta hai, isliye alag wording par bhi high score de sakta hai. Lekin isme spelling errors bhi high score le sakte hain. Rule: classification/extraction me precision/recall/F1, translation me BLEU + human review, summarization me ROUGE + BERTScore + human review, open-ended generation me LLM judge + human review.
Q27RAG evaluation me retrieval aur generation ko alag kyun naapte hain?
Kyunki dono me se ek bhi kharab ho to final jawaab kharab hoga — aur fix alag hoga. Retrieval metrics: hit rate (sahi doc top-k me aaya ya nahi), MRR (pehla sahi result kis rank par), MAP (ranking quality), precision/recall. Generation metrics: faithfulness (jawaab retrieved context se support hota hai ya invent kiya), answer relevance, context precision/recall. Agar retrieval achha hai lekin jawaab galat hai to generation (prompt/model) fix karo; agar retrieval hi galat hai to chunking/embedding/reranking fix karo. Bina alag measurement ke tum andhere me teer chala rahe ho.
Q28Prompt injection kya hai aur RAG systems me ye khaas khatarnak kyun hai?
Prompt injection ek attack hai jisme attacker model ko malicious instruction dekar uska behavior hijack kar leta hai. Direct injection: user seedha kahe 'apne instructions bhool jao'. Indirect injection: malicious instruction kisi document ya webpage me chhupi ho, jise model padhe — user ne kuch galat nahi kaha, lekin model compromised document padh kar attacker ki baat maan leta hai. RAG me ye khaas khatarnak hai kyunki retrieved documents me injection chhupa ho sakta hai. Bachav: input validation, output filtering, least privilege, retrieved documents ko untrusted treat karna (unki information use karo, instructions follow mat karo) aur monitoring.
Q29NIST framework ke hisaab se LLMSecOps audit ke 10 steps kaun se hain?
10 steps hain: (1) Scope aur objectives define karo, (2) Information gather karo, (3) Risk analysis aur threat assessment, (4) Security controls evaluate karo, (5) Penetration testing / red teaming, (6) Model training aur data review karo, (7) Model performance aur bias assess karo, (8) Monitor aur review karo, (9) Findings aur recommendations document karo, (10) Results communicate karo aur remediation plan banao. Audit team diverse honi chahiye — ML engineers, security specialists, domain experts, product/risk managers, legal officers, external auditors. Cost: external audit (steps 1-6) $25,000-$250,000, internal (steps 7-10) $5,000-$50,000, regulatory deep audit $500,000+ tak.
Q30RBAC kya hai aur LLM applications me ye kyun zaroori hai?
RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) ka matlab hai har user ko ek role dena (admin, editor, viewer) aur har role ko specific permissions dena. LLM app ke frontend me RBAC se hota hai: permissions manage karna aasan hota hai, least privilege enforce hota hai (har user ko sirf utni access jitni zaroori hai), aur audit me pata chalta hai ki kisne kya kiya. Principles: least privilege, separation of duties (critical actions par do approvals), regular permission review, aur audit logs. Bina RBAC ke, ek compromised account ya ek careless user poori system ko nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai.
Q31Model drift kya hai aur use kaise pakdein?
Drift wo phenomenon hai jab model ki performance dheere-dheere girti hai bina kisi ko pata chale. 3 types: data drift (input data badal gaya — naye words, topics), concept drift ('sahi' ka matlab hi badal gaya — jaise policy update), model drift (provider ne model update kar diya — same prompt par alag output). Pakdne ke tareeke: eval set ko continuously chalao (score girte hi alert), input distribution monitor karo, output quality monitor karo (response length, refusal rate, user feedback), aur embedding drift dekho. Feedback loops se system sudharta hai — user feedback ko eval set, RAG docs aur prompts me wapas dalo, lekin blindly trust mat karo.
Q32Data, model aur pipeline parallelism me kya farq hai?
Data parallelism: dataset ko chunks me baanto, har GPU ko ek chunk do, har GPU par model ki copy rakho — gradients average karke update karo. Simple hai, lekin model ek GPU me fit hona chahiye. Model parallelism: model ko hi baanto — har GPU ko kuch layers do. Memory problem solve hoti hai, lekin throughput ghatti hai kyunki ek GPU kaam kare to dusre wait karte hain. Pipeline parallelism: model ko layers me baanto aur data batches ko micro-batches me todo — saare devices ek saath busy rahte hain. 4 devices par 4 micro-batches ka example kitab me hai. PiPPy (ab PyTorch me merged) isse implement karna aasan banata hai.
Q33ZeRO aur DeepSpeed kya hain aur ye kab use karein?
ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer) training ke dauraan memory overhead kam karta hai — model states (parameters, gradients, optimizer states) ko devices par partition karke, duplicate store karne ki jagah. Isse tens ya hundreds of billions parameters wale models train ho sakte hain bina huge-memory GPUs ke. DeepSpeed ZeRO par built ek library hai jo mixed-precision training, gradient accumulation aur memory optimization deti hai — training time aur cost dono kam hote hain. Use karo jab model ek GPU me fit na ho ya training bahut mehenga ho. Chhote models ke liye zaroorat nahi — pehle quantization aur gradient accumulation try karo.
Q34Full, incremental aur differential backup me kya farq hai?
Full backup: poora dataset ya model ek point-in-time par capture karo — restore simple hai (ek backup se ho jata hai) lekin storage zyada lagta hai. Incremental backup: sirf wo changes jo pichle backup ke baad hue — storage kam lagta hai, lekin restore ke liye poori sequence chahiye; ek bhi block missing ho to restore fail hoga. Differential backup: wo changes jo pichle full backup ke baad hue — restore ke liye latest full + latest differential chahiye; storage aur speed ka balance hai. High-stakes apps me frequent full backups, bade data me incremental/differential. Aur sabse important: backup lena kaafi nahi — restore ko har quarter test karo, kyunki untested backup kaam nahi karta.
Q35LLMOps engineer ke roop me succeed karne ke liye kya chahiye?
Technical skills: Python, APIs, Docker, Kubernetes, cloud, CI/CD, monitoring (foundation), plus LLM-specific — prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, evaluation, vector DBs (har saal update hote hain). Systems thinking: poora system dekho — model, data, infra, security ek saath. Non-technical: communication (technical cheezein simple bhasha me samjhana), documentation (decisions, incidents, runbooks), incident handling (pressure me calm, systematic debug, blameless postmortem) aur business sense (har decision ka cost/revenue/risk impact). Career: MLOps/software se shuru karo, production LLM systems own karo, phir architecture aur strategy ki taraf badho. Field tez badal raha hai — seekhna kabhi band mat karo.
Q36LLMs ka future kya hai — hybrid architectures aur LLMOps ki kya role hogi?
Future hybrid hoga: neurosymbolic (neural + logic), memory-augmented models (external memory), MoE (experts), multimodal fine-tuning, cross-model collaboration, meta-learning (seekhna seekhna), self-optimizing models aur sparse models. Scaling compute-optimal hoga — bada model nahi, sahi balance (model size + data). Inference-time compute badhega — model ko 'sochne' ka zyada time. Data, privacy (on-device LLMs, confidential computing) aur regulations aur important honge. LLMOps ki demand badhegi — kyunki systems aur complex honge. Jo skills is kitab me hain — data, deployment, evaluation, governance, scaling — ye aane wale saalon me aur valuable honge.
